Olmsted County by the numbers

Which Olmsted County department sends and collects the tax bill?

The Property Records and Licensing department in the Government Center at 151 4th Street SE, Rochester, runs both the billing side and the valuation side. Questions about a statement go to 507-328-7636, and prior-year delinquent balances go to 507-328-7635. Payment by mail goes to PO Box 6681, Rochester, MN 55903-6681.

The county's own property tax FAQ explains that the tax is the property's value multiplied by the total rate of the district it sits in, with residential homesteads getting a market value homestead exclusion. Value and class come from Assessing Services, reached at 507-328-7670 on weekdays.

Property Records and Licensing also offers eNoticesOnline, a free service that delivers the tax statement and valuation notice by email in place of paper, with a Pay button that links to the county's payment portal. A tax statement carries more than the county's share. School district, city or township and special taxing districts such as watersheds all take a cut, along with any tax increment financing diversion and special assessments for street work.

What does Olmsted County look like for a home seller?

Olmsted County is the state's seventh-most populous county, and almost all of that weight sits in one city. Rochester, the county seat, is Minnesota's third-largest city and lies in the Zumbro River valley at the center of the county. Stewartville, the second-largest, has about 6,000 residents. Outside the valley the land is farmland and small towns, with no suburbs touching the city. The county has eight cities, including Byron, Eyota, Oronoco and Dover, and school districts such as Rochester Public Schools (ISD 535), Byron (531), Stewartville (534) and Dover-Eyota (533).

The county was created in 1855 with Rochester as its seat, and its boundaries have not changed since. The Zumbro, Whitewater and Root rivers drain it, and like Mower, Pipestone and Rock counties it has no natural lakes. Interstate 90, U.S. 14, 52 and 63, and Rochester International Airport tie it to the region.

Census QuickFacts figures:

  • 166,731 people in July 2025, up 2.4% since the 2020 base
  • 74,363 housing units, 70.6% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $331,700 and median gross rent of $1,370
  • Median household income of $95,406, with 49.4% of adults holding a bachelor's degree or more
  • 542 building permits issued in 2025
  • Health care and social assistance receipts of about $3.03 billion in 2022, with 107,285 jobs at employer firms in 2023

The $331,700 median value sits well above neighboring Mower County's $185,200, so the same tax rate produces a larger dollar bill here. Knowing the November Truth-in-Taxation notice and the two installment dates keeps cash flow predictable for a landlord or an estate holding a house in Rochester or one of the smaller cities.

What are the Olmsted County installment dates?

The county's 2026 dates follow the property type, and a due date on a weekend moves to the next working day. A postmark on a mailed payment counts.

Olmsted County 2026 tax installments, from the Revenue and Records page
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Houses, commercial buildings and personal propertyMay 15, 2026October 15, 2026
Agricultural real estateMay 15, 2026November 16, 2026
Manufactured homesAugust 31, 2026November 16, 2026

The Truth-in-Taxation notice that previews next year's tax goes out in November, so it is arriving now. It can differ from the real bill because it leaves out special assessments and does not reflect referendums. An owner who occupies a property by December 1 can file for homestead for the following year, and the county shows December 15 as the homestead application date.

How can I pay an Olmsted County bill?

Your parcel ID is required with every form of payment. The paying page lists these options:

  • Online by credit card or e-check, at 3.28% for cards and $3.16 for e-checks, for current-year tax only, with a $300,000 ceiling
  • Bank bill pay, which counts as paid on the day the county receives it, often seven to ten days after the bank issues it
  • Automatic withdrawal (ACH), withdrawn May 10 and October 10, or November 10 for agricultural property; not offered on mobile homes
  • In person at the Government Center, or by mail

The county charges $2 for each reprint of a statement at its office. For ACH, the 2026 sign-up cutoffs were April 10 for the first half and September 11 for the second, and a form that misses a cutoff rolls to the next payment cycle. An online payment can take seven to ten business days to clear the bank, so do not wait for the last day.

How do I appeal an Olmsted County valuation?

Gather an appraisal, a recent sale of a similar house or other evidence, then call the Assessor at 507-328-7670 or visit 151 4th Street SE. The valuation notice goes out in mid-March. If the conversation does not settle it:

  1. Attend the local board of appeal listed on your notice, which begins in mid-April, or the open book meeting if your area uses one. A jurisdiction with no local board goes straight to the county board.
  2. Attend the County Board of Appeal and Equalization. In 2026 it met on June 23 and asked owners to book a time at 507-328-6001.
  3. Petition the Minnesota Tax Court by April 30 of the year taxes are payable.

Since the 2023 change to Minnesota Statutes 278.01, a petition must be served on the county auditor. Olmsted County accepts service by email at olmcotaxpetitionservice@olmstedcounty.gov, or in person at the County Attorney's Office, 151 Fourth Street Southeast, and issues an acknowledgement.

How is the tax split when an Olmsted County house sells?

Statements are mailed in late March, and a mid-year buyer receives none, so the county tells new owners to look the bill up online. At closing the county's guidance is that tax is prorated, with the seller covering January up to the closing date and the buyer covering the rest of the year. A seller who prepaid the full year is reimbursed by the buyer for the buyer's portion.

One quirk affects sellers: an overpayment made at closing can belong to the previous owner, and the county sends any refund to the party that made the payment. The county also mails a homestead application to new owners after a transfer.

Unpaid tax turns delinquent the following year, goes into judgment, and a residential homestead forfeits to the State of Minnesota after three years. Under section 272.12 the auditor must confirm no delinquent tax before a deed is recorded, so any back balance has to be paid off at or before closing.

More questions about Olmsted County, MN Property Tax Guide

Which Olmsted County second-half dates apply in 2026?

October 15, 2026 for most real estate, and November 16, 2026 for agricultural parcels and manufactured homes. The earlier October date has already passed. Contact 507-328-7636 about any balance.

Which office answers Olmsted County value questions?

Call Assessing Services at 507-328-7670. The office is at 151 4th Street SE in Rochester and stays open weekdays until 4 p.m. Bring recent sales or an appraisal if you plan to dispute the value.

Will I get a tax statement if I buy mid-year in Olmsted County?

No. Statements are mailed in late March and are not sent for mid-year purchases. You can find the bill on the county website or at its office, and not receiving one does not excuse a late payment.

How do I serve a tax court petition on Olmsted County?

Email the petition to olmcotaxpetitionservice@olmstedcounty.gov before the April 30 deadline, or hand it to staff at the County Attorney's Office, 151 Fourth Street Southeast. The county will send back an acknowledgement of service.

Can I set up automatic tax payments in Olmsted County?

Yes for most parcels, but not for mobile homes. Submit the ACH form with a voided check; money comes out May 10 and October 10, or November 10 for agricultural property. A form that misses the cutoff rolls to the next cycle.

Think of the Assessor as the office for arguing about worth, and the Auditor/Treasurer as the office for learning what you owe on the day you list the house.

What kind of county is Sherburne for a seller?

Sherburne belongs to the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan statistical area and counts Elk River as both seat and biggest city. Of its 451 square miles, 433 are land. Low hills, scattered lakes and sandy, gravelly glacial soil make up the terrain, and that soil is less suited to farming than much of Minnesota. The Mississippi forms the southern boundary and the Rum River cuts through the upper east side.

County government began at Humboldt, the village that later took the name Big Lake, before a county vote moved the seat to Elk River in 1867. Incorporated cities now include Baldwin, Becker, Big Lake, Clear Lake, Elk River and Zimmerman, with Princeton and St. Cloud partly inside the line. Census QuickFacts supplies the housing picture:

  • Population reached 104,194 in July 2025, a 7.2% rise over the April 2020 base.
  • The county holds 38,457 housing units, and owners live in 83.2% of the occupied ones.
  • A typical owned home was worth $361,400 across 2020 to 2024.
  • The usual household brings in $105,466 a year and drives 30.7 minutes to work.
  • Renters pay about $1,127 a month in gross rent, and households average 2.78 people across 35,555 homes.
  • Builders pulled 319 permits in 2025 across roughly 225 residents per square mile.

Lakes, rivers and the Sherburne National Wildlife Refuge all lie within the county, so setting can move a parcel's value as much as the house does.

When do Sherburne County property taxes come due, and what do late payments cost?

Mark May 15 and October 15. Farmland owners get until November 15 for the second half. The county counts a mailed check as on time only if the postmark falls on or before the deadline, and it cautions that many post offices now stamp mail two or three days after pickup. A real estate bill of $50 or less has just one deadline, May 15.

Penalties begin the day after each deadline and rise month by month. This is the 2026 schedule for a first half left unpaid:

Sherburne County first-half penalty by date, 2026 (county Penalties page)
Date reachedHomestead or cabinNon-homestead
May 162%4%
June 14%8%
July 15%9%
October 18%12%
January 2 of the following year10%14%

An unpaid second half starts at 2% for homesteads and 4% for everything else on October 16. Farm homesteads that miss the November deadline owe 6%, and non-homestead farmland owes 8%. Owners paying late should ask the property tax division for the exact penalty before sending money.

What are my options for paying Sherburne County tax?

The county's payment page lays out five routes. Checks go to the Sherburne County Auditor / Treasurer at the Elk River address. The property tax division in the Government Center also takes cash or check at the counter, and a drop box by the main entrance (door A) stays open after hours.

  • Forte, online or at 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307: 2.40% of the tax (minimum $2.00) on credit cards, $1.55 per eCheck, $4.00 on a debit card. Keep the parcel ID handy.
  • Direct payment: withdrawals on May 15 and October 15, or November 15 for farmland. Forms must arrive by April 15 for the spring withdrawal and September 15 for the fall one, and a cancellation has to meet those same cutoffs.
  • Lender escrow: if your mortgage payment includes tax, the lender sends it. Confirm with your servicer.

A withdrawal that lands on a weekend or bank holiday happens the following business day.

How can I contest a Sherburne County value or class?

Gather evidence first, such as a recent appraisal or sales of similar homes, and talk it over with the Assessor. If that does not settle things, attend the local board shown on your valuation notice. The county's 2026 list ran from early April, when Big Lake and Princeton hearings took place at the Government Center on April 3, to Livonia Township on April 27, so this year's round is over.

  • Local board: meets at the city or township hall in April, with the exact date printed on your notice.
  • County board: sat Tuesday, June 16 in 2026 at 3:00 p.m., by appointment only, arranged through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351.
  • Minnesota Tax Court: you may petition directly after receiving the notice, up to April 30 of the year the tax is payable (court phone 651-296-2806).

Next spring's notice will carry the new dates. The Assessor also runs an online tool at gis.co.sherburne.mn.us/AssessmentSchedule that shows the year an appraiser will inspect an address, since every property needs a physical review once in five years.

The Assessor's property values page explains what is being tested. Minnesota statutes call for estimated market value to sit at 100% of market, so appraisers review current sales continuously and note any physical change that affects land or buildings. A new deck, a finished basement or a demolished garage all belong in the conversation, because they alter what the appraiser should have on file.

Errors discovered afterward can be corrected through an abatement request to the Assessor. The county lists three kinds: homestead (you must show you lived there), valuation and classification, and a local option for a house where disaster damage reaches half the structure's value. Pay on schedule meanwhile, because review can take months.

How does a sale change my Sherburne County tax responsibilities?

Any unpaid balance gets cleared at the closing table, normally out of your proceeds. Phone the Auditor/Treasurer for the amount due on the parcel, and ask your lender what sits in escrow if one collects your tax.

Selling a homesteaded house also creates a duty. The county cites Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e): report the sale, transfer or change of primary residence to the Assessor within 30 days. An online change-of-address form is posted on the county site. Request a copy of the current statement from the Auditor/Treasurer too, as the title company will want the parcel figures.

More questions about Sherburne County, MN Property Tax Guide

Which dates should I remember for Sherburne County real estate tax?

May 15 and October 15, with agricultural parcels paying the second half on November 15. A bill of $50 or less is entirely due May 15. Postmarks decide whether a mailed check is on time.

What is the Sherburne County Assessor's phone number?

763-765-4900. The office works from 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, and it deals with value, class, abatements and the opening stage of any appeal.

Does Sherburne County accept credit cards for tax?

Yes, through Forte online or by calling 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307. Expect 2.40% on credit cards with a $2.00 floor, $1.55 on eChecks and $4.00 on debit cards, shown before you confirm.

Where does a county board of appeal hearing take place in Sherburne County?

At the Sherburne County Government Center in Elk River. Owners who stayed unhappy after their local board must book through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351. In 2026 it met June 16.

What must I report after selling my Sherburne County homestead?

Tell the Assessor within 30 days, as Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e), requires. Call 763-765-4900 with questions.

Who to contact in Chisago County

Tax rate

Chisago County by the numbers

Which Chisago County office bills property tax?

The Auditor-Treasurer's Office in Center City calculates, bills and collects every property tax bill in Chisago County. It sits at 313 N Main Street, Room 271/274, and answers at 651-213-8500 from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday except holidays. Center City is also the county seat.

The same office handles property combinations and splits, records land transfers so names and addresses stay current, tracks special assessments, runs the tax forfeiture process and settles collected money with the local governments. Homestead applications and valuation questions go to the county assessor instead.

When do Chisago County statements arrive, and what if I never got one?

Real estate statements go out by March 31, and manufactured home statements by July 15. They also appear online one to two weeks after mailing. The statement is the only notice you get, and its two bottom stubs carry the first-half and second-half due dates.

Statement files are generated in mid-February for the owner of record at that moment. Anyone who bought later receives no statement, and the county still holds the owner responsible for knowing when taxes are due. Download a copy from the county's property tax page or call for one. The county adds that statements go to the owner whether or not a mortgage escrow account exists, and the owner must know whether the lender or the owner pays.

When is Chisago County property tax due?

Tax under $100 and all personal property is due in full on May 15. Larger bills may be paid in two installments, and the dates depend on the property class.

  • Real estate: May 15 and October 15
  • Agricultural: May 15 and November 15
  • Mobile home: August 31 and November 15
  • Personal property: May 15

Mailed payments count as on time only with a postmark on or before the due date. The county urges anyone paying near a deadline to take the envelope to the post office and ask the postmaster to postmark it.

How much penalty does a late second half carry in Chisago County?

The county publishes a separate table for each property type. This one covers the second-half payment on residential homestead and cabin property, plus the case where both halves are unpaid.

Penalty on unpaid second-half tax, Chisago County homestead and cabin property
Not paid beforeSecond half onlyBoth halves unpaid
October 162%5%
November 14%6%
December 15%6.5%
January 27%8.5%

Source: Chisago County Due Dates & Penalties page. Non-homestead rates run higher: a first-half payment made after October 1 carries 12%, and 14% after January 2.

Penalty stops when a bill turns delinquent on the first business day of January. Interest then starts under Minn. Stat. 270.03 at 8% a year, charged as simple interest each month on the tax, penalty and publication fee.

What happens when Chisago County taxes go delinquent?

Taxes unpaid from a prior year are delinquent. By February 15 the county auditor files the delinquent list with the district court administrator, a step the county ties to Minn. Stat. 279.05. Minn. Stat. 279.09 then has the list published in the county's official newspaper by March 20, with a second printing at least two weeks later. Chisago County charges $25 per parcel to recover that cost.

  • Only full payment of all delinquent tax removes a parcel from the list.
  • Partial payments are encouraged because they cut the balance and the interest, but they do not stop forfeiture.
  • If the balance is not paid by the end of the redemption period, usually three years but it varies by class, the property can be forfeited.
  • Anyone near the end of that period should call the office to ask about options.

How do I get homestead status or sell a mobile home in Chisago County?

An owner who lives in the home as a primary residence, or whose qualifying relative lives there, applies to the county assessor on the Homestead Application. Completed forms are due by December 31, either in person or by mail. The county page also lists tracks for relative homestead, disabled veteran, manufactured home, special agricultural, blind or disabled (class 1b) and first-time home buyer. A spouse may claim a separate homestead in cases such as pending dissolution, legal separation or a job that keeps the spouse at least 50 miles away.

Moving or selling a mobile home takes a Tax Release Letter signed by the Auditor-Treasurer showing no tax owed. The seller must show a current title in the seller's name first, and the buyer takes both the title and the letter to a Minnesota motor vehicle office. The nearest is the Chisago City DMV.

How does the Chisago County appeal process work?

In March the assessor mails a Valuation and Classification Notice that lists market value, class, new improvements and exclusions such as homestead. Call the assessor first. Most Chisago County communities then hold a Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, and an owner who still disagrees may go to the County Board of Appeal and Equalization. You can appeal value and classification, but not the tax itself.

Every parcel is valued as of January 2, and appraisers visit each property about once every five years. For the January 2, 2026 assessment, the assessor used sales from October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025, and each sale's Certificate of Real Estate Value helps separate open-market sales from bank-owned or family transfers. Under Minn. Stat. 274.01, an owner who was told of a proposed increase and neither appeared nor wrote to the local board cannot go on to the county board. For budget complaints, use the Truth in Taxation meetings or the annual township meeting.

What should a Chisago County seller check before listing?

Pull the current statement and confirm that both halves are paid or scheduled. The county site has an online property search for recent and prior years, an interactive GIS map, a property tax calculator and an address change form for statements. Updating the mailing address matters most after you sell, since the owner of record gets the next statement.

Check the class on your statement too. A homestead classification lowers tax, and the buyer will have to apply for it separately. Parcels with forfeited or delinquent history should be cleared first, because only full payment takes a parcel off the delinquent list. When in doubt, call 651-213-8500 and ask for the amount owed through a specific date.

What does Chisago County look like for a house seller?

Chisago County runs 415 square miles of land along the St. Croix River and the Wisconsin border, and the Census Bureau estimates 59,142 residents for July 2025. Its cities are Center City, Chisago City, Harris, Lindstrom, North Branch (the largest), Rush City, Shafer, Stacy, Taylors Falls and Wyoming. The Chisago Lakes area groups Shafer, Chisago City, Lindstrom and Center City. Interstate 35 and U.S. Highway 8 serve the county.

  • Median owner-occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $351,900
  • Owner-occupied rate: 85.9%
  • Households: 21,364
  • Median household income: $99,400
  • Mean commute: 31.0 minutes
  • Building permits, 2025: 240

Each city runs its own council, and the county posts each council's meeting schedule. Andersen Corporation, the window and door maker, is among the large manufacturers named for the county.

More questions about Chisago County, MN Property Tax Guide

When are Chisago County property taxes due?

Real estate taxes are due May 15 and October 15. Agricultural property pays the second half on November 15, and mobile homes pay on August 31 and November 15.

What if my Chisago County tax statement never came?

You still owe the tax. The county generates statements in mid-February for the owner of record then, so a buyer after that date gets none. Print one from the county website or call 651-213-8500.

What interest does Chisago County charge on delinquent tax?

Interest starts on the first business day of January and runs at 8% a year, as simple interest charged monthly. It applies to the tax, penalty and publication fee.

How long before Chisago County can forfeit my property?

Unpaid tax goes through a redemption period that varies by class and usually lasts three years. Only full payment stops forfeiture, so call the office before the period ends.

How do I apply for homestead in Chisago County?

File the Homestead Application with the county assessor, in person or by mail, by December 31. The owner must live in the home as a primary residence, or a qualifying relative must.

Selling in Otter Tail County? Get a Cash Offer

Who to contact in Otter Tail County

What we could not confirm

  • Millage/tax rate not collected

Otter Tail County by the numbers

Who values and who collects in Otter Tail County?

The county's government offices are at the Government Services Center, 500 West Fir Avenue, Fergus Falls, MN 56537. The Assessor handles value and class at 218-998-8010. The Treasurer takes payments and questions at 218-998-8295, the Auditor can be reached at 218-998-8030, and the Recorder, who files deeds, is at 218-998-8140.

The Assessor's page says appraisers review about 65,000 parcels across 62 townships and 22 cities. They run annual sales studies, and the Minnesota Department of Revenue requires the county's estimated values to land between 90% and 105% of actual market value. Notices go out each spring with the dates for appealing.

The Assessor's Office also mails each owner a notice in spring with a new value and class. With that many parcels, classification choices carry weight. The department sorts property by primary use, such as residential, agricultural, seasonal or commercial, and a lake cabin is taxed differently from a year-round house.

What is Otter Tail County like for a seller?

Otter Tail County covers 2,224 square miles, of which about 253 are water, making it Minnesota's seventh-largest county by area. Its 1,048 lakes are more than any other county in the United States, according to Wikipedia, and the county's own site says it has over 1,000. Fergus Falls is the seat and largest city. The county was created in 1858 and organized in 1868, and the seat moved from Otter Tail City to Fergus Falls after an 1872 vote. Other cities include Perham, Pelican Rapids, Battle Lake, Henning, New York Mills and Parkers Prairie. Becker, Clay, Wadena, Todd, Douglas, Grant and Wilkin counties surround it, and school districts include Fergus Falls, Battle Lake, Henning, Frazee-Vergas and Detroit Lakes. Inspiration Peak, at 1,727 feet, is among the highest points, and six small municipal airports, at Fergus Falls, Perham, Battle Lake, Henning, Pelican Rapids and Wadena, serve light aircraft.

Census QuickFacts figures:

  • 61,041 people in July 2025, with 27.6% aged 65 or older
  • 37,036 housing units but only 25,157 households, and 79.5% of occupied units owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $273,000 and median gross rent of $868
  • Median household income of $72,255, with 72 building permits in 2025
  • Land area of 1,971.63 square miles and about 30.5 people per square mile

The gap between housing units and households is large, which is a reminder that many county parcels are not a primary residence. Whether a parcel counts as homestead or seasonal changes the rate and the penalty schedule, so check the class on your notice before you set a price.

What does the Otter Tail County tax calendar look like?

The county posts one calendar covering assessment, appeals and payment, and a Saturday or Sunday due date slides forward to the first business day after it. The entries that matter most to an owner:

Selected Otter Tail County property tax dates from the county calendar
DateEvent
January 2Assessment date for real and personal property
April 30Deadline for a Tax Court petition on value
May 15First half of real property tax; also first half of agricultural tax
May 31First half for resort and certain seasonal commercial property
August 15Deadline to file a Property Tax Refund Return
October 15Second half of real estate tax, unless part is agricultural
November 15Second half for classes 1b, 2a and 2b agricultural property and manufactured homes
December 31Final date to establish homestead for the current year

The Treasurer does not mail second-half statements and will not accept post-dated checks. Whatever the class, the penalty rates come from section 279.01, which charges 2% on homestead and 4% on nonhomestead property for a missed date.

How can I pay the Otter Tail County Treasurer?

The payment options page sets out the choices:

  • Online by e-check at $1.00 per transaction, or by card at 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum; enter the parcel number without the leading R, P or M
  • Automatic withdrawal, using the county's Automatic Withdrawal Form returned to the Treasurer
  • Mail, with checks payable to Otter Tail County and a U.S. Postal Service postmark as proof of timely mailing
  • In person at the Treasurer's counter, or in the drop box at the entrance during business hours, with another drop box in the parking lot for after-hours payments

Third-party bill pay should be started early so the checks carry the right dates. A private postage meter mark does not count, and the county suggests having the post office hand-cancel the envelope when in doubt.

How does an Otter Tail County value appeal work?

The county lays out a sequence on its appeals page. Read both sides of the valuation notice, which arrives in March and April, then call the Assessor.

  1. Present the case to your Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, made up of the township board or city council. The county's calendar shows these boards convening April 1 to 20.
  2. Where the area holds an Open Book meeting instead, contact your appraiser from the Contact My Assessor list.
  3. Take it to the countywide board, which convenes in June on up to ten meeting days after the second Friday.
  4. File with the Minnesota Tax Court. The county says this is open even to owners who skipped the earlier steps, and the deadline is April 30 of the taxes-payable year.

Property owners may also serve a petition on the county auditor under 278.01. Resort owners watch an earlier date: January 15 is the last day to submit for class 1c or 4c(5) resort classification.

What if the tax goes unpaid before I sell?

After three years of unpaid tax measured from the judgment year, a parcel defaults to State of Minnesota ownership, and the Auditor-Treasurer then sells it to the highest bidder at public sale. The county's current page lists a sale dated November 16, 2026 with 18 tracts, including houses in Deer Creek, Fergus Falls, New York Mills and Pelican Rapids, with starting bids from $100 to $30,000.

Anyone owing delinquent real or personal property tax in the county is barred from bidding. Staff cannot arrange viewings of forfeited property before a sale. Sale proceeds above the minimum bid can be claimed by interested parties within six months of the first notice of surplus, under Minnesota Statutes 282.005, and the county page shows one such claim period running to February 25, 2027.

For an ordinary sale, section 272.12 has the auditor certify whether delinquent tax is due before a deed is recorded. Ask the Auditor at 218-998-8030 for the payoff figure well before the closing date, and the Recorder at 218-998-8140 about filing.

More questions about Otter Tail County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the Otter Tail County Treasurer's phone number?

The Treasurer is at 218-998-8295 in the Government Services Center, 500 West Fir Avenue, Fergus Falls. The Assessor, who answers value and classification questions, is at 218-998-8010.

When is the Otter Tail County second-half tax due?

October 15 for ordinary real estate and November 15 for classes 1b, 2a and 2b agricultural property and manufactured homes. A date falling on a weekend moves to the next business day. The county does not mail second-half statements.

What are the Otter Tail online payment fees?

An e-check costs $1.00 per transaction, and a credit or debit card costs 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum. Enter the parcel number without the R, P or M prefix. Paying by check or in person adds no fee.

Who handles Otter Tail County resort and seasonal property classification?

The Assessor's Office. Owners seeking class 1c or 4c(5) resort classification must apply by January 15, and the county lists May 31 as the first-half date for seasonal commercial property. Call 218-998-8010 with questions.

Can I still appeal to the Tax Court if I skipped the local board?

Yes. The county states the Minnesota Tax Court is open even to owners who did not use the earlier steps. The petition deadline is April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

  • Cass County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Who to contact in Cass County

Selling in Cass County?

Who collects and assesses property tax in Cass County?

The Cass County Auditor-Treasurer collects the tax at the courthouse, 303 Minnesota Avenue W, second floor, in Walker. Phone (218) 547-7260 and mail to PO Box 3000, Walker, MN 56484. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm. Besides property tax, the department runs elections, vital statistics, licensing and the parcel mapping system.

Value and classification belong to the county assessor at (218) 547-7298. Cass uses one county-wide assessment system, so every parcel in every township is valued from the same office rather than by local assessors. Staff appraisers view each property about once every five years and look at all new construction and alterations in the current year.

When are Cass County property taxes due?

The first half of real property tax is due May 15, and the non-farm second half is due October 15. Farm real property and manufactured homes pay their second half on November 15. A deadline that falls on a weekend or legal holiday slides forward to the following business day, and personal property taxes share the real property schedule.

Cass County tax due dates by property type
Due dateWho pays
May 15Real property, first half (or the whole bill if it is $100 or less)
May 31Resorts, first half
August 31Manufactured homes, first half (or all if $50 or less)
October 15Non-farm real property, second half
November 15Farm real property and manufactured homes, second half

Source: Cass County Property Tax Payment Due Dates page.

The May 31 resort date comes from Minn. Stat. 279.01, which extends the date to commercial seasonal recreational property in classes 1c and 4c and to class 3a property that earns over 60 percent of its gross income in May through August. A class 3a owner attaches an affidavit, and the county asks eligible businesses to return its Commercial Tax Deferral Form.

How can I pay a Cass County tax bill?

The county's payment page lists these routes:

  • At the courthouse during office hours.
  • By mail to the Cass County Auditor-Treasurer with the right stub, postmarked before the due date. The second-half stub sits directly above the first-half stub at the bottom of the statement.
  • Autopay through MuniciPay. An ACH payment costs $1.00 and a card costs 2.25% of the payment with a $1.00 minimum.
  • By phone at (218) 321-9802, with a confirmation number noted down.
  • Through a mortgage escrow account. If a lender pays the bill, the statement copy you get reads that taxes paid by an escrow agent should not be paid again.

Electronic payments take about two business days to post, so do not wait for the due date. The county suggests asking the local postmaster to hand-stamp a mailed envelope near a deadline. Fees on electronic payments go to the service provider, not the county.

What is the Cass County refuse management fee?

Cass County charges a flat refuse management fee on improved parcels with an assessed value of at least $1,000. The charge began in 1990, was once called the solid waste fee, and funds waste disposal and recycling programs. The county board has kept it as a flat fee instead of folding the cost into the levy.

  • Residential and seasonal properties: $86
  • Commercial under $9,999 in building value: $86
  • Commercial from $10,000 to $99,999: $195
  • Commercial from $100,000 to $499,999: $391
  • Commercial at $500,000 and up: $652
  • Apartments: $16 per unit
  • Non-commercial tax-exempt buildings: $86

Any improved parcel you sell will carry this line, so factor it into what the buyer's first bill looks like.

How do I question my Cass County value or homestead?

The notice of assessed value mailed each spring explains how to appeal. The assessor's office answers questions all year at (218) 547-7298. Local boards of appeal sit between April 1 and May 31 under Minn. Stat. 274.01, and anyone who is told of a proposed increase and fails to show up or write in may not go on to the county board.

Market value is set as of January 2 each year. The state expects an assessor's value to land between 90% and 105% of sale price, and the county says it has stayed within that range. File a homestead application with the assessor. The same office can tell blind or disabled owners and disabled veterans whether they qualify for the relief Minnesota offers them. The refund program for homeowners is run by the state, so Cass County staff direct those questions to the forms and instructions from the Department of Revenue.

What should a Cass County seller do about the tax record?

Tell the Auditor-Treasurer your new mailing address as soon as you move. The county warns that a wrong address can delay or block time-sensitive statements and other property mailings, and care-of addresses can be added. It also says no owner name is changed in the tax records without a recorded legal document.

Sellers working through a contract for deed should read the county's Property Tax Billing and Collection Procedures fact sheet, which explains who receives the statement.

What happens to unpaid taxes and tax-forfeited land in Cass County?

Interest begins on unpaid balances after January 2 of the following year, and penalties and rates follow state statute. Partial payments are accepted on prior-year taxes, with a $100 minimum preferred. The money goes to the newest year first and then back through earlier years. The county states that nonpayment results in loss of the property through forfeiture under Minnesota law.

Cass County's Land Department manages about 255,000 acres of tax-forfeited land, with timber sales, reforestation and wildlife management on it. Call the Auditor-Treasurer at (218) 547-7260 for the amount past due on a parcel. If you sell on a contract for deed, only the new contract holder receives the bill, but the seller still has to watch that the taxes get paid.

What sets Cass County apart for a house seller?

Cass County is large and quiet: 2,022 square miles of land plus 393 of water, and a 2025 population estimate of 31,430. Walker holds the courthouse, and Lake Shore is the biggest city. Much of the Leech Lake Indian Reservation lies in the county, and Chippewa National Forest and Crow Wing State Park reach into it. Winters are cold: the Walker January average low is 0 degrees F.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 25,344
  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 12,874
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $288,300
  • Median household income: $68,874
  • People 65 and older: 29.8%

The gap between 25,344 housing units and 12,874 households points to a large stock of seasonal and second homes, and the statute puts class 4c seasonal recreational property on the homestead penalty schedule. Anyone listing a lake cabin in a township such as Pine River, Shingobee or Boy Lake, should check the class on the statement and the payment dates that go with it.

More questions about Cass County, MN Property Tax Guide

What are the Cass County payment deadlines?

May 15 for the first half of real property and October 15 for the second half of non-farm property. Farm real property and manufactured homes pay the second half on November 15, and resorts have until May 31.

Can I pay Cass County property tax online?

Yes, through MuniciPay. ACH costs $1.00 per payment and a debit or credit card costs 2.25% with a $1.00 minimum. Allow two business days for posting.

Where do I send a Cass County tax payment?

Send it to the Cass County Auditor-Treasurer, PO Box 3000, Walker, MN 56484, with the stub from your statement, or bring it to the courthouse at 303 Minnesota Avenue W.

What is the $86 charge on a Cass County tax statement?

It is the refuse management fee that applies to residential and seasonal parcels with an assessed value of at least $1,000. It pays for waste disposal and recycling in the county.

Who decides my Cass County homestead status?

The Cass County Assessor's Office reviews homestead applications. Call (218) 547-7298 to apply or to check the status.

We buy Crow Wing County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Crow Wing County

  • Crow Wing County Land Services / Tax
  • Crow Wing County Land Services handles assessment and appeals.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • E-check and credit/debit cards accepted; 3-4 days processing for online payments; call 218-824-1010 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Crow Wing County by the numbers

Who runs property tax in Crow Wing County?

One department, Land Services, both assesses and collects in Crow Wing County. You will find it at 322 Laurel Street in Brainerd, the seat of the county, and its phone line is 218-824-1010.

Land Services mails bills, takes payments, answers valuation questions and keeps the field books and parcel records that the public can research on the lower level of its building. The county's Property Search website shows parcel data, and a duplicate tax statement can be pulled there by parcel ID or address.

What should a seller know about Crow Wing County's housing stock?

This is lake country in east central Minnesota: 999 square miles of land, about 417 named lakes, the Mississippi cutting through, and gently rolling wooded ground. Census estimates for July 2025 show 69,132 residents, a gain of 4.6% since the 2020 base.

  • Communities on the county's list include Brainerd, Baxter, Crosby, Crosslake, Garrison, Nisswa, Pequot Lakes, Breezy Point, Deerwood and Fort Ripley.
  • The Census Bureau counts 44,306 housing units and 29,402 households, and Wikipedia's 2020 figures show 32.9% of housing units vacant, which points to a large stock of cabins.
  • Owners live in 77.0% of occupied homes, and the typical home among them is worth $306,800 (2020 to 2024).
  • A typical household earns $72,589, and 26.8% of residents have passed 65.
  • Builders took out 625 permits in 2025.

Brainerd began in 1870 when the Northern Pacific Railroad picked the site for its Mississippi River crossing, and it took the county seat from the earlier trading village of Crow Wing. Because so many parcels here are lakeshore, classification matters: a homestead and a seasonal cabin are taxed under different rules.

What are the Crow Wing County payment dates?

The first half of a real estate bill falls due May 15 and the second half October 15. Farmland gets until November 15 for its second half. Mobile homes are billed on August 31 and November 15.

Resorts and businesses that earn more than 60% of gross income between May and August can file an affidavit to push the first-half date to May 31, and the affidavit must accompany the payment. All 2026 real estate dates have now passed, so any balance from this year is already carrying penalty.

A bill unpaid on December 31 of its due year turns delinquent. For delinquent years, the county asks you to call Land Services at 218-824-1010 before paying so you pay the right amount, and it notes that payments are applied to the newest years first under Minnesota Statutes section 280.39.

How steep is the Crow Wing County late penalty?

Penalties come from a state-set table that the county posts, and an unpaid first half climbs the fastest. The county's own figures for that half are below.

Penalty on an unpaid first half, Crow Wing County Land Services table
DateHomestead and cabinsNon-homestead
May 162%4%
June 14%8%
July 15%9%
August 16%10%
September 17%11%
October 18%12%

Manufactured homes carry an 8% penalty from September 1 on the first half, and personal property is at 8% from May 16. State law also allows the treasurer to abate the penalty one time for a mailed check postmarked within a business day of the deadline.

Where and how can you pay in Crow Wing County?

Land Services accepts four kinds of payment.

  • Online: E-check costs $1.95 and a card costs 2.35% of the payment or $1.95, whichever is greater, with a $50,000 limit. The processor collects those fees, not the county, and credit takes three to four days to post.
  • You need the 8-digit parcel number for each parcel, and a full year is paid by choosing Pay Full Year.
  • At the counter: weekdays from eight in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon, with an outside drop box that never closes.
  • By mail: send the remittance stub and payment to Land Services, 322 Laurel Street Ste 15, Brainerd, MN 56401.

How are Crow Wing values set, and how do you push back?

The office revalues every parcel yearly and must land between 90% and 105% of market value. Staff walk each property once in five years and check permits. Comparable sales drive the number, adjusted for land, size, quality and condition, and the class follows how the property is used today.

The county lays out two routes. Route one runs through the boards: a local board or open book meeting first, then the county board, which requires a call ahead to be placed on its agenda. A city or township with no local board sends owners to an open book session before the county board. Route two is the Minnesota Tax Court.

  • Meeting times and places are printed on your Notice of Valuation and Classification.
  • You may appear in person, send a letter, or use a representative you authorize.
  • A court petition has an April 30 filing date for the year the tax is payable (section 278.01).

Which tax relief programs does Crow Wing point to?

The county's Taxes page links to Minnesota Department of Revenue guidance for owners who may qualify for a lower bill. Several of them depend on filing before a deadline, so ask Land Services which ones fit your parcel.

  • Homestead classification and the homestead market value exclusion for owner-occupied houses.
  • Special homestead classification for owners who are blind or disabled.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferral.
  • Market value exclusion for veterans with a disability.
  • 2c managed forest land and the Sustainable Forest Incentive Act.
  • Green Acres and rural preserve deferral for agricultural and rural vacant land, plus special agricultural homestead.
  • Property tax refunds.

A seller who is behind on tax can also pay part of a bill. The treasurer may accept less than the full installment, and under section 279.01 the money goes to the oldest unpaid installment first. A payment that falls short is applied to accrued penalty before tax. A partial payment does not waive the minimum payment needed to keep an appeal alive.

How does a Crow Wing sale treat unpaid tax?

Delinquent tax blocks recording: the auditor has to clear the land first (section 272.12). A sale over $3,000 also brings a certificate of real estate value (section 272.115), and the seller's homestead class drops off until the buyer applies and qualifies.

Ask Land Services for a payoff figure for each parcel, since a lake property sale often includes several. The assessing office also lists tax relief programs that can matter to a new owner, such as 2c managed forest, disabled veterans, Green Acres, homesteading and rural preserve.

More questions about Crow Wing County, MN Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Crow Wing County property taxes?

You pay Land Services at 322 Laurel Street Ste 15 in Brainerd, online, by mail or in a drop box. The counter is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone is 218-824-1010.

What are the Crow Wing County due dates?

Real estate is due May 15 and October 15, agricultural second half on November 15, and mobile homes on August 31 and November 15. The 2026 real estate dates have passed, so the next one is the first half in May 2027.

How much is the late penalty on a Crow Wing County homestead?

It starts at 2% on an unpaid first half after May 15 and reaches 8% by October 1, according to the county's table. Non-homestead property starts at 4% and tops out at 12%.

Can I challenge my Crow Wing County valuation now?

The local and county board meetings for the 2026 value are finished. A Tax Court or district court petition on taxes payable in 2027 is due April 30, 2027, so call Land Services at 218-824-1010 and ask for the assessor.

Do delinquent Crow Wing County taxes need to be paid before a sale?

Yes, delinquent taxes must be cleared before the deed can be recorded. Call Land Services at 218-824-1010 before paying them online, because the county wants staff to confirm the right amount and avoid extra penalty. Delinquent years can also be paid in person or by check or money order after that call.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Isanti County

What we confirmed on official pages

Isanti County by the numbers

Which Isanti County offices bill and value my house?

The work divides between two county offices: the Assessor sets value and classification, and the Auditor-Treasurer bills and collects. Mail for the Assessor goes to Isanti County Assessor, 555 18th Avenue SW, Cambridge, MN 55008.

The Isanti County Assessor estimates the market value of every parcel and decides its classification under Minnesota statutes and Department of Revenue standards. The same page carries the forms for agricultural use, homestead, local option disaster abatement, managed forest and the disabled veterans market value exclusion. Cambridge holds the county seat, and a seller who has a question about a bill, a classification or a payoff should start with these two counters before anyone else.

What does Isanti County look like before I price a house?

Isanti County is a growing exurban county in east-central Minnesota, and the Census numbers show it. Mid-2025 Census estimates show 44,386 residents, a 7.9% rise over the 41,128 counted as the April 2020 base.

The county was formed on February 13, 1857, has roughly 436 square miles of dry land, and sits inside the Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington metropolitan area. The Rum River runs south through its middle. The cities are Cambridge, Isanti, Braham (partly in Kanabec County) and St. Francis (mostly in Anoka County). Anoka County borders it on the south, which is why many owners commute to the metro. Census figures put the mean trip to work at 30.7 minutes, longer than in the other three counties covered in this series.

  • Housing units: 18,068 in July 2025, and 276 building permits were issued during 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 83.7% for 2020 to 2024, so most sellers here are owners of long standing.
  • Census 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes: $306,200.
  • Median household income: $87,440, with median gross rent at $1,273.

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer for the exact figure on your parcel, because the median says nothing about your own bill.

Who owns homes in Isanti County, and where do they live?

Owners occupy most Isanti County homes, and the county mixes town and country. The 2020 census counted 15,615 households and 16,550 housing units, with 5.6% of units vacant and 82.5% of occupied units owner-occupied.

Wikipedia's county summary adds that 40.7% of residents lived in urban areas and 59.3% in rural areas, where the median resident was 39.6 years old. The terrain is hilly, cut by gullies and dotted with lakes and ponds, and the highest point is near the northwest corner at about 1,020 feet. Neighbors are Kanabec, Pine, Chisago, Anoka, Sherburne and Mille Lacs counties.

  • Small parks and wildlife areas include Maywood County Park, Springvale County Park and the Twin Lake Scientific and Natural Area.
  • Rural parcels can sit in agricultural, managed forest or Green Acres programs, each with its own application date on the county calendar.
  • Agricultural use has to be in place by January 2 of the assessment year to count for the following payable year.

For a seller, the rural and urban mix matters because the assessor's classification of the parcel feeds directly into the tax calculation.

When are Isanti County property taxes due?

Most residential and agricultural owners pay the first half by May 15 and the second half by October 15, with agricultural second halves moving to November 15. Manufactured homes follow a different calendar.

Isanti County property tax due dates by classification
Due dateWhat is due
May 15First half, residential and agricultural
August 31First half, manufactured homes (whole bill if $50 or less)
October 15Second half, residential only
November 15Second half, manufactured homes and agricultural

Source: Isanti County Auditor-Treasurer, Due Dates and Penalties. A mailed payment counts as on time if its postmark is dated no later than the due date, and all personal property tax is payable in full by May 15.

What does a late payment cost in Isanti County?

Miss a due date and Minnesota law adds a percentage penalty that grows each month. Under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01, the first penalty is 2% on homestead property and 4% on nonhomestead property.

Leave the installment open into the following month and the same percentage lands again. After that, one more percent is added at the start of each month until December. The total stops at 8% for a homestead and 12% for a nonhomestead parcel. A rental house or a vacant inherited home usually falls in the higher group, so an estate holding an Isanti County house that has been left unpaid for a few months can see a double-digit penalty.

The statute also says the treasurer must forgive the penalty once if a payment is mailed and postmarked within one business day of the due date, provided the owner has not used that relief before.

What is the path to contest an Isanti County valuation?

Start with the assessor, then the local board of appeal and equalization in your city or township, then the county board. Court is the last step.

For a court challenge, Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 gives two doors. A petition to district court has to be served on the county auditor and filed with the court administrator by April 30 of the calendar year in which the bill comes due. A Tax Court appeal can be started after the valuation notice arrives and before May 1 of that same year. The county's local board page shows meeting dates on its calendar, and the November 2026 calendar lists no meetings, so check back in the spring after notices are mailed.

Appealing does not excuse payment. Section 279.01 says the treasurer may take partial payments and that doing so does not waive the minimum payment required to keep an appeal alive under section 278.03. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer what that minimum is before you file.

Which Isanti County application dates matter to a homeowner?

The assessor's application calendar runs on the assessment year, and an application filed late usually takes effect a year later. The county lists these cutoffs:

  • Homestead, plus actively farming or special agricultural homestead: December 31.
  • Blind or disabled special homestead: October 1.
  • Mobile home homesteads: May 31.
  • Green Acres, Rural Preserve, managed forest land and nonprofit community service organizations: May 1.
  • Exempt properties: July 1. Sustainable forest: September 30.

Source: Isanti County Application Deadlines. Agricultural use must be in place by January 2 of the assessment year to apply to the following payable year.

Separately, the state's Homestead Credit Refund carries an August 15 filing date, and Revenue accepts a claim for a year beyond it.

How are taxes handled when I sell an Isanti County house?

The tax bill stays with the parcel, so unpaid tax has to be settled at or before closing. Ask the Isanti County Auditor-Treasurer for the amount due on your parcel number, including any penalty and any special assessment.

If a lender escrows your taxes, the lender pays on your behalf and the statement will say not to pay it yourself. When you sell, the purchase contract decides how the current year is split between buyer and seller. Bring the most recent statement and the closing date to the treasurer's office so the payoff matches what the title company will request.

More questions about Isanti County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the second half deadline for a regular Isanti County home?

October 15 for a residential property. The county lists agricultural and manufactured home second halves on November 15, and a mailed payment counts as on time if postmarked by the due date.

Where is the Isanti County Assessor located?

The Assessor accepts applications by mail at 555 18th Avenue SW, Cambridge, Minnesota 55008. The county seat is Cambridge as well.

Can I appeal my Isanti County value after the spring meetings?

Yes, through court. A district court petition has an April 30 filing deadline in the payable year, and a Tax Court appeal can start after the valuation notice arrives and before May 1, under Minnesota Statutes section 278.01.

How much is the late penalty on an Isanti County rental house?

It starts at 4% on a nonhomestead parcel and can reach 12% by December, under section 279.01. A homestead starts at 2% and tops out at 8%.

When should I file for homestead in Isanti County?

By December 31 of the assessment year for it to apply to taxes payable the next year. Blind or disabled special homestead has an October 1 cutoff.

Selling in Goodhue County?

What we could not confirm

Goodhue County by the numbers

What is Goodhue County like for a home seller?

Goodhue County sits in southeastern Minnesota on the Wisconsin border, across Lake Pepin, with Red Wing as the county seat. The legislature carved it out of Wabasha County on March 5, 1853, and it was named for James Madison Goodhue, who published the first newspaper in the territory. Wheat built the early economy, and for several years the county led the country in wheat output. Today the ground is rolling hills and bluffs cut by the Cannon River, and traffic runs on U.S. 52, 61 and 63.

Census QuickFacts gives a picture of the housing a seller is dealing with:

  • 48,195 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 1.3% since the 2020 census.
  • 19,727 households, with 78.8% of homes lived in by their owners.
  • A median owner-occupied home value of $285,100 and a median household income of $84,171.
  • 84 building permits in 2025 across 21,445 housing units.

Cities include Red Wing, Cannon Falls, Zumbrota, Kenyon, Wanamingo, Goodhue and pieces of Lake City and Pine Island. Red Wing Public Schools, Cannon Falls, Zumbrota-Mazeppa and Kenyon-Wanamingo are among the school districts that levy on county homes.

Which Goodhue County office handles property tax?

Finance and Taxpayer Services runs both the assessor and the auditor/treasurer from the second floor of the Government Center, 509 W. 5th St. in Red Wing. The phone is 651-385-3040 and the counter is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. For assessor questions, choose option 1.

The county reminds owners that its board controls only the county budget and levy. Of thirteen reasons a bill can move, which include a change in your value, a shift in other owners' values, city or township levies, school levies, referendums, special assessments and state aid or law changes, only the county piece belongs to the commissioners. A seller who sees a jump should check which piece moved before calling.

When are Goodhue County property taxes due?

Minnesota Statutes 279.01 splits the bill into two halves, payable before May 16 and before October 16 when the tax on a parcel is over $100. Agricultural homestead and qualifying farm land may pay the second half without penalty through November 15.

Penalty starts at 2 percent on homestead and 4 percent on nonhomestead on the day after a due date. It is repeated on the first of the next month, then 1 percent monthly through December, topping out at 8 percent for homestead and 12 percent for nonhomestead. The treasurer must abate a late penalty once if the envelope was postmarked within one business day of the due date and the owner has not used that abatement before.

Owners can search records and pay from the Finance page link labeled Search Property Tax Records/Pay Property Tax, and the office can quote a payoff for a parcel before closing.

How does Goodhue County arrive at my value?

The assessor estimates market value and classification for more than 29,000 parcels as of January 2, and the figure sets taxes payable the following year. Staff try to view the inside and outside of each home, list size, age, quality, basement finish and extras, and feed that into a mass appraisal system that a county appraiser reviews. Sales from October 1 through September 30 before the assessment date are the guide.

State rules require every property to be physically reviewed at least once every five years and require the overall level of assessment to land between 90 and 105 percent of market value. The county says it consistently meets that test. Classification matters as much as value: homestead, nonhomestead residential, apartment and commercial are each taxed at a percentage set by the legislature. The county is also doing on-site reassessments in several areas during 2026, so a seller whose neighborhood is on that list should expect a visit request.

Do values and rules differ across Goodhue County?

They can. The county spans ten cities, either whole or in part, and 21 townships, and each has its own levy on top of the county and school district levies. A house in Red Wing and a farmhouse in Vasa Township share a county assessor, yet they face different local boards, different school districts and sometimes different reassessment schedules. Part of the county touches Dakota County to the northwest and Olmsted to the southeast, and Prairie Island Indian Community lies almost entirely within the county.

The assessor's notice for 2026 says on-site reassessments are under way in a number of areas. If you get a letter asking for an interior viewing, answering it gives the appraiser accurate facts about finish, condition and extras, which is easier than arguing about them after the notice arrives. The county adds that owners who think the value and classification on their notice are right do not need to contact the assessor at all.

How do I appeal a Goodhue County assessment?

Start with facts. Pull recent sales of comparable homes and any market analysis, then call the assessor at 651-385-3040 option 1 and walk an appraiser through them. An interior inspection can be scheduled. If the question is still open, go to the local board of appeal and equalization, then make an appointment with the county board. The county board listing shows a June 15 meeting by appointment only, and the call to book it goes through the same number.

Goodhue County appeal path, from the county assessor's appeal page
StepWhereDetail
1AssessorGather sales, call 651-385-3040 option 1, review with an appraiser
2Interior inspectionSchedule if the appraiser asks
3Local boardAttend the meeting for your city or township
4County boardAppointment only, 509 W. 5th St., Red Wing
5Minnesota Tax CourtPhone 651-539-3260; filing deadline April 30

Only the current year valuation can go through the boards. The county says an appeal of a prior year value runs through Tax Court alone, and Statutes 278.01 sets April 30 of the tax year as the court filing date.

What should I check in Goodhue County before listing?

  • The valuation notice mailed in March, for the estimated market value and the class assigned to the home.
  • Whether the home is still classified as homestead for the owner who is selling.
  • Whether the neighborhood is in the 2026 reassessment group.
  • Both halves of the current year tax, and any older balance on the parcel.
  • Whether any appeal is pending, since Tax Court filings for a tax year close on April 30.

Finance and Taxpayer Services can answer the tax and assessor items at 651-385-3040, and the title company handles the payoff once a buyer is under contract.

What happens to the tax bill when I sell a Goodhue County house?

Delinquent tax comes first. Under Minnesota Statutes 272.12 the auditor checks a deed for delinquent tax before transfer, and the recorder will not file it without the auditor's note. If the sale covers only part of a parcel, Statutes 272.121 calls for the treasurer's certification that the full-parcel tax for the current year is paid.

For an ordinary whole-parcel sale, ask the title company how this year's first and second halves will be split, and ask Finance and Taxpayer Services for the amount still open on the parcel. Buyers who plan to live in the home should apply for homestead; the county assessor's notice says people who bought or moved into a property in the past year may qualify for a property tax refund.

More questions about Goodhue County, MN Property Tax Guide

Who sets property values in Goodhue County?

The county assessor, working from the Government Center in Red Wing. Values are set as of January 2 and mailed to owners in March. Call 651-385-3040 option 1 with questions.

When is the Goodhue County board of appeal and equalization?

The county page lists June 15, by appointment only. Call 651-385-3040 option 1 to book a time before then, after trying the local board for your city or township.

Can I appeal last year's Goodhue County value?

Only through Minnesota Tax Court. The county says prior year values cannot go to its boards, and the court filing must be made by April 30 of the year the taxes are due.

What are the Goodhue County tax due dates?

Half is due before May 16 and half before October 16, per Minnesota Statutes 279.01. Qualifying agricultural property can pay the second half by November 15 without penalty.

Do I need to pay delinquent tax to sell my Goodhue County home?

Yes. A deed cannot be recorded until the auditor certifies no delinquent tax remains, so the payoff is normally handled at closing by the title company.

What should a McLeod County, MN owner know about property tax before selling?

Two offices decide what a parcel owes. The assessor picks the value and the class, and the Auditor-Treasurer in Glencoe converts those into a bill and collects it.

Before listing, confirm three items: the current half is paid, no special assessment is attached, and you know what happens to the homestead class at closing. Each can shift what a seller nets, and a phone call settles each one.

  • Auditor-Treasurer, 520 Chandler Avenue North, Glencoe: 320-864-1203 for payments and 320-864-1271 for tax balance questions.
  • County Assessor: 320-864-1254 for valuation, class and homestead forms.

Where is McLeod County and who lives in its homes?

McLeod County sits west of the Twin Cities in south central Minnesota. It covers 506 square miles, about 491 of them land, and it was created by the territorial legislature on March 1, 1856. Glencoe holds the courthouse, while Hutchinson has the most people. Biscay, Brownton, Lester Prairie, Plato, Silver Lake, Stewart and Winsted round out the list of cities. The South Fork of the Crow River crosses the upper middle of the county, and low rolling hills and small lakes mark the rest of the farmland.

The 2020 count was 36,771 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 36,631. Of the 16,162 housing units QuickFacts lists, 77.4% of occupied ones are owned. A typical owned home was worth $246,100 across 2020 to 2024, and a typical household brought in $80,084. Builders took out 206 permits in 2025. Census data for 2020 put 55.5% of residents in urban areas and 44.5% in rural areas, so a seller might hold a Hutchinson lot, a farmstead near Brownton or a lake cabin, and each is taxed in its own class.

When is McLeod County property tax due?

Regular real estate and personal property tax is due May 15 and October 15. Farmland follows a later calendar, and manufactured homes use their own dates. McLeod County lists the schedule this way:

McLeod County annual property tax due dates (McLeod County Auditor-Treasurer, Due Dates page)
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estate and personal propertyMay 15October 15
Agricultural propertyMay 15November 15
Manufactured homesAugust 31November 15

Statements go out in March, with a statutory mailing deadline of March 31. Manufactured home statements are scheduled for June, with a July 15 deadline. An owner who has not received a statement still has to pay, so call the Auditor-Treasurer for a duplicate. A seller who is mid-transaction should ask for a copy early, because the buyer's lender and the title company will want to see the parcel number and the amount.

How can I pay McLeod County property tax?

The county offers six payment methods. Pick with the closing calendar in mind.

  • In person by check or cash at the Government Center in Glencoe.
  • By mail, made out to McLeod County Auditor-Treasurer. Mail needs a postmark by the due date, and the county cautions that servicing centers can stamp it two or three days after you drop it off.
  • Online or by phone with a credit card or eCheck. The card fee is 2.5% of the transaction. eChecks cost $1.50 under $10,000 and $10.00 above that.
  • The secure drop box in front of the Government Center. Anything inside at 8:00 a.m. counts as the previous day's business.
  • Direct debit from a bank account, which must be set up at least one month before the due date.
  • Mortgage escrow, where the lender pays from the account it holds.

In the online search, type just the numeric part of the parcel ID and pick the roll type from the drop-down.

What happens if a McLeod County tax payment is late?

Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets the schedule. A half that is still open after its date picks up 2% on a homestead or 4% on other property, then the same again at the start of the next month, then 1% monthly through December. Ceilings are 8% for homestead and 12% for nonhomestead. McLeod County sends owners to the state sample tax statement for the current table.

A year becomes delinquent in the following calendar year, and interest and penalty then keep building each month while the parcel heads toward judgment and forfeiture. The office takes payments above or below the exact installment, and a short payment covers that year's penalty first. A one-time abatement is available when a mailed payment carries a postmark within one business day of the due date and the owner has not used that relief before.

Who sets my value in McLeod County, and how do I appeal it?

Sue Schulz is the McLeod County Assessor. Her office sets market value and class, and the Auditor-Treasurer applies the local rate to it. A deputy assessor and four appraisers divide the county by area. The deputy assessor handles Hutchinson plus every apartment and commercial parcel, an appraiser covers Glencoe, Lester Prairie and Winsted, and the staff page lists who covers each township and smaller city. The Department of Revenue requires every property to be viewed, and the county says a visit takes about 15 minutes or less. An owner can decline the inspection and the appraiser then judges value from outside.

Challenges move up three steps under Minnesota Statutes chapters 274 and 278:

  • Local board of appeal and equalization: your town board or city council sits sometime from April 1 to May 31 and wraps up within 20 days. Its combined reductions cannot cut the assessor's total by more than one percent.
  • County board: the commissioners and the auditor take what the local board left open. Owners who ignored a notice at the local level may be barred from this stage.
  • Tax Court or district court: file the petition and proof of service before the end of April in the year the bill is payable.

A call to the assessor with a few comparable sales is the cheapest first move.

Which relief programs can lower a McLeod County tax bill?

For most owners the homestead class is the biggest saving. McLeod County says occupying the property by December 1 lets an owner apply for the following year. A closing resets it: under 272.115 the assessor drops the homestead class after a transfer unless the buyer applies and qualifies. A buyer who forgets will see a bigger bill the next year, so raise it during negotiation.

The county's FAQ also covers state refunds. Someone who lived in the property as a homestead on January 2 may get a refund scaled to household income and tax paid, and a second, special refund exists where the bill jumped by more than 12 percent in a year. Form M-1PR claims both, and the Department of Revenue answers form questions at 651-296-4444.

How do taxes work when a McLeod County house sells?

Recording a deed in Minnesota depends on the tax record. Section 272.12 has the auditor look for delinquent taxes before moving the land on the books, and a recorder who skips that step commits a gross misdemeanor. A deed that conveys only part of a parcel needs the treasurer's word that this year's tax on the whole parcel is paid (272.121). Sales above $3,000 also need a certificate of value (272.115).

Find out from the closing agent how this year's tax will be split, and from your lender what becomes of any escrow balance. Special assessments for streets and similar improvements appear as a separate line on the statement and follow the benefit to the parcel, so ask the Auditor-Treasurer what remains unpaid on a parcel before you settle on a price.

The November Truth in Taxation notice previews next year's tax. It omits special assessments, and a passed referendum can raise the final number.

More questions about McLeod County, MN Property Tax Guide

Which McLeod County office answers tax questions?

The Auditor-Treasurer handles bills and payments at 320-864-1203 or 320-864-1271, and the Assessor handles value, class and homestead at 320-864-1254. Both sit in the Government Center at 520 Chandler Avenue North in Glencoe.

What are the McLeod County property tax due dates?

Regular real estate is due May 15 and October 15. Agricultural property is due May 15 and November 15, and manufactured homes are due August 31 and November 15. Statements are mailed in March.

Can I pay McLeod County taxes by credit card?

Yes, online or by phone. The vendor adds 2.5% of the total for cards, and eChecks run $1.50 below $10,000 or $10.00 above. Cash, check, the drop box, direct debit and escrow are also accepted.

Does a McLeod County sale cancel the homestead classification?

It does for the next assessment year unless the buyer files a homestead application and qualifies. State law has the assessor strip the class after a transfer, and the owner is expected to report the sale within 30 days.

When must a McLeod County value dispute reach court?

The petition is due by April 30 of the payable year. Work through the local board in April or May and then the county board first, because skipping those steps after notice can cost you the right to appear.
