Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Wabasha County

  • Wabasha County Auditor/Treasurer

Tax rate

Selling in Wabasha County?
We buy Wabasha County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where do I take a Wabasha County tax bill?

The Auditor/Treasurer's counter sits at 625 Jefferson Avenue in the city of Wabasha, with weekday hours from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon. The Assessor shares that address and answers questions about value and class at 651-565-3669. To get a copy of a statement, ring 651-565-2648, or use the Beacon lookup linked from the county's statement page with a parcel number or street address.

The payment page offers several routes:

  • The web at www.co.wabasha.mn.us/paytax, or the phone line 1-866-539-2020 (bureau code 8190128) between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. Monday to Friday; keep the parcel number and amount handy, and expect a convenience fee from the card processor
  • Direct Payment Plan (ACH) drafts from a checking or savings account, with forms at the office or through 651-565-4410
  • The brown mailbox-style drop box standing in front of the courthouse
  • A mailed check with the stub, bearing a postmark that is not later than the due date
  • A visit to the counter with cash, check, money order, e-check or a card

If you move, even for a short stay, give the county the new address. The Post Office returns undeliverable statements and notices to the courthouse rather than forwarding them.

Who owns houses along the Mississippi in Wabasha County?

Wabasha County lines the Mississippi River in southeastern Minnesota and takes in part of Lake Pepin. It was one of nine counties the territorial legislature created on October 27, 1849, and the boundaries have been fixed since 1855. The city of Wabasha is the seat. Lake City, partly across the Goodhue line, is the biggest city. Plainview, Mazeppa, Elgin, Kellogg, Hammond, Millville, Zumbro Falls, Bellechester and Minneiska complete the list of cities.

Low hills cut by creek drainages cover most of the ground, and the Zumbro and Whitewater rivers cross it. Carley State Park and the Kellogg-Weaver Dunes natural area sit within its protected land. Rochester's metro area includes the county, but 81.2% of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census. Census QuickFacts supplies these figures:

  • 21,537 people in July 2025, 0.8% above the 2020 base
  • 10,439 housing units, with 83.3% lived in by their owners
  • $264,400 as the median home value, and $1,763 in monthly owner costs where a mortgage exists
  • $830 median gross rent, against a median household income of $82,007
  • Only 51 building permits in 2025, and 25.4% of people at 65 or over

Few new houses arrive and the population skews older, so sellers here often hold an inherited farmhouse, a retiree's place or a home left empty after a move. Each of those still needs a clean tax record before the deed goes to the recorder.

When do Wabasha County property taxes come due?

Real estate is payable in two parts. A due date that lands on a weekend moves to the Monday after it, per the county's own note. The October 15 date for ordinary real estate is behind us.

Wabasha County payment calendar, as posted by the Auditor/Treasurer
Type of propertyFirst paymentSecond payment
Real estate, most classesMay 15October 15
Classified agriculturalMay 15November 15
Mobile (manufactured) homesAugust 31November 15
Prior-year tax left unpaidTurns delinquent January 2

Statements are mailed at the end of March, and mobile home statements follow, with July 15 as the assessor's mailing deadline for those. Someone who buys after the mailing gets no statement. The office sends a courtesy letter with the year's tax, and it does so even when a lender is paying out of escrow.

What does paying late cost in Wabasha County?

Minnesota Statutes 279.01 adds 2% to a missed homestead installment and 4% to a non-homestead one. A matching amount lands on the first of the following month, then 1% per month after that, topping out at 8% for homestead and 12% for non-homestead. The reverse side of the county statement prints its own table.

Wabasha County says plainly that it does not waive these penalties, since the rates come from the Legislature. About two weeks after a missed date the office mails a courtesy notice with the tax owed and the penalty accrued. The statute carves out one exception: mail postmarked within a single business day of the deadline gets the penalty abated, once per owner. Tax still open on January 2 is delinquent, and that balance follows the parcel into any sale.

How can I dispute a Wabasha County value?

The county values property as of January 2. Market value notices go out in March, April and May, at least ten days ahead of the local board meeting, and those local boards sit from April 1 through May 31. A phone call to the assessor at 651-565-3669 comes first, and it also covers questions on why a home lost its homestead class.

  1. Appear before the board in your city or township, if one exists, with an appraisal or recent comparable sales.
  2. Move up to the county-level board, which meets in the final ten meeting days of June after the second Friday. The valuation notice prints the times.
  3. Or file in Minnesota Tax Court. The petition must be served on the county auditor under section 278.01, and the assessor's calendar sets April 30 as the final filing date for current taxes.

Mobile homes taxed as personal property run on a separate clock: September 1 is the Tax Court deadline for a valuation petition.

How does a Wabasha County closing handle the tax bill?

Before the recorder accepts a deed, the auditor looks for delinquent tax. Section 272.12 bars recording unless the document carries the note that no delinquent taxes are due. Any back tax must be paid by the time of signing. Ring the Auditor/Treasurer at 651-565-2648 for the balance while the date is still open.

The split of the current year between seller and buyer comes out of the purchase agreement and the closing statement, so confirm it with the title agent or attorney. Heirs clearing out a parent's house should note that statements travel to the address on file, which may be a house nobody is checking mail at anymore.

Which other filing dates can a Wabasha County homeowner use?

The assessor's dates and deadlines page names several that have nothing to do with the two payments:

  • February 1: filing an exemption from taxation
  • May 1: Green Acres deferment for the next year's taxes
  • July 1: disabled veterans homestead exclusion and the senior deferral
  • August 15: the state Property Tax Refund, form M-1PR
  • October 1: special homestead class for the blind or the permanently and totally disabled
  • December 31: establishing homestead for the current assessment

Proposed-tax notices are mailed by November 24, which is about now. Local governments then hold budget hearings from November 29 through December 20, and that is the stage at which a resident can speak on next year's levy.

More questions about Wabasha County, MN Property Tax Guide

Which Wabasha County tax date is coming up?

Monday, November 16, 2026, for second-half agricultural and mobile home tax, since November 15 is a Sunday. Ordinary real estate was due October 15. For a balance, call 651-565-2648.

Do new buyers in Wabasha County get a statement in the mail?

No, if the purchase happens after the March mailing. A courtesy letter with the year's tax arrives instead, whether or not a lender escrows. Confirm the figure with the Auditor/Treasurer.

Does the county ever forgive a late fee?

Rarely. The county states that state law fixes the rates, so it does not waive them. The statutory exception covers a payment mailed with a postmark within one business day of the deadline, once per owner.

Whom should I ask about a jump in my assessed value?

The Assessor, at 651-565-3669, in the courthouse at 625 Jefferson Avenue in Wabasha. Gather an appraisal or comparable sales first, because the office will usually want to inspect the property.

By when must a Tax Court petition be filed in Wabasha County?

April 30 for current taxes on real and personal property. A mobile home assessed as personal property has a September 1 deadline. In both cases the county auditor must be served.

Winona County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

Who to contact in Winona County

Tax rate

Selling in Winona County?

Winona County by the numbers

How do I pay a Winona County property tax bill?

The Auditor-Treasurer's office is on the main floor of the Winona County Office Building, 202 West Third Street in Winona, and opens from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Checks are made out to the Winona County Auditor-Treasurer, and the phone number for tax questions is 507-457-8830. The county's property taxes page describes the options below.

Winona County payment methods and what each one costs
MethodCost to the taxpayerNotes
Credit card online2.4% convenience feeCharged by the card processor, not the county
Debit card online1.5% convenience feeSame processor
Electronic check onlineFlat $1.50Online, through the county's payment link
Check by mail or drop boxNone listedInclude the stub; the drop box is on the Washington Street side
Automatic ACHNone listedPulls from your account on the due date; call to enroll

One practical point from the FAQ: the exterior deposit slot and the counter box inside are closed after each tax due date. Penalty is added the next day, so after a deadline you must come inside, call, or look up the amount online before paying.

A lost statement is easy to replace. Open the county's Beacon page from the pay online link, search by parcel number (the xx.xxx.xxxx digits on your statement) or by address, and scroll to the Tax Statement section, where the last few years appear as PDF links. An address change can be filed on the county's online form, by calling 507-457-8830, or on the back of a payment stub.

What sets Winona County apart for a seller?

Winona County hugs the Mississippi River along Minnesota's eastern edge, in the driftless country of the southeast. The legislature carved it out on February 23, 1854, mostly from northern Fillmore County with a small slice of Wabasha, and the lines have not moved since. Winona is both the seat and the largest city. The county has 13 cities in all, among them Goodview, Lewiston, St. Charles, Rollingstone and Altura, while La Crescent sits mostly in Houston County. The land climbs to about 1,365 feet on a hill east of Wilson, and Winona's municipal airport is named Max Conrad Field.

Two colleges, Winona State University and Saint Mary's University of Minnesota, give the city a college-town feel. Census QuickFacts gives these figures:

  • 50,523 residents in July 2025, 1.7% above the 2020 base
  • 22,003 housing units, only 69.5% of them owner-occupied
  • $235,400 as the median owner-occupied value and $907 as median gross rent
  • $70,744 median household income, with 13.3% of residents in poverty
  • A short 17.6-minute average commute, and just 42 building permits in 2025

With nearly a third of households renting at the 2020 census (31.9%), a lot of Winona sellers are landlords. Their tax bills run on the same schedule as an owner-occupant's, but a rental generally lacks homestead status, which shifts both the class and the penalty tier.

When are Winona County taxes due this year?

The Auditor FAQ lists three schedules, with a note that dates may shift slightly if they fall on a weekend:

  • Real estate: May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second
  • Agricultural property: May 15 and November 15
  • Mobile homes: August 31 and November 15

The October 15 deadline for houses has gone by. Anyone behind should call 507-457-8830, because under section 279.01 a penalty starts accruing the day after the due date.

If your lender escrows, the payment stub will say so and the lender learns the amount by file or printout. Do not forward the statement to the mortgage company. Keep it for your records.

How does Winona County set my home's value?

The Assessor's department, at 202 West Third Street and 507-457-6300, values property with a computerized mass appraisal system built on sales. For a house it weighs square footage, bedrooms and bathrooms, age and condition, basement finish, garage size, fireplaces and the land. State standards allow values between 90 and 105 percent of market, measured across all sales and not any one house.

Per the county's FAQ, market swings usually move a value more than improvements do. Added rooms, a finished basement, a major kitchen or bath remodel, new siding or windows, and central air all raise it. Painting, a new water heater, shingling a roof or repairing porch steps generally do not, though several together might. For a seller that is useful: small repairs before listing are unlikely to change the tax value, and the assessor's number is not the same thing as an offer price.

How do I challenge a Winona County valuation?

The county advises phoning the assessor after the late March valuation notice. Staff will explain how the figure was reached and may ask to inspect the house. Formal appeal meetings follow in April. The county board then sat as the Board of Appeal and Equalization on June 16, 2026, and its agenda page lists the session.

A Tax Court route also exists. Under section 278.01 the petition goes on the county auditor and must be filed with the court administrator by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-457-8830 how the office accepts service of a petition.

What does the county say about taxes at a Winona County closing?

The Auditor's FAQ describes the typical sale this way: taxes are prorated and the buyer is credited with the seller's share, which you confirm on the closing statement or with the realtor or attorney. Delinquent tax has to be paid at closing, and current tax does not. Under section 272.12 the recorder cannot take a deed without the auditor's notation that no delinquent taxes remain.

Mobile homes need an extra step. The sale calls for a county statement saying all delinquent and current taxes are paid in full, which comes from the Auditor-Treasurer. A seller holding a stray statement should hand it to the new owners, who need it to pay.

What homestead and refund rules apply in Winona County?

Homestead treatment requires that the owner or a qualifying relative own and live in the home as the principal residence. Ownership and occupancy must be in place by December 1 of the year before taxes are payable, and a new homestead application is due by December 15. The assessor's page offers regular and relative homestead forms, a special classification for the blind or disabled, Green Acres paperwork and a mold damage reduction form.

A Property Tax Refund requires state form M1PR, available at the county office or from the Minnesota Department of Revenue at 651-296-4444 or 800-657-3676.

More questions about Winona County, MN Property Tax Guide

Where is the Winona County tax drop box?

On the Washington Street side of the Winona County Office Building at 202 West Third Street, to the right of the entry doors. A second box sits on the counter inside. Both are closed after each due date.

Does Winona County charge a fee to pay by card?

Yes, through its payment vendor: 2.4% for credit cards, 1.5% for debit cards and a flat $1.50 for e-check. The county neither charges nor receives those fees. Checks and ACH carry no listed fee.

Do I have to pay Winona County taxes at closing?

Only delinquent tax must be paid at closing. Current-year tax is normally prorated, with the buyer credited for the seller's portion, but the closing statement controls. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-457-8830 for any status check.

What paperwork does a Winona County mobile home sale need?

The county's own statement confirming that all delinquent and current taxes are paid in full. Request it from the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-457-8830 before you schedule the closing.

What is the Winona County homestead application deadline?

December 15 for a new homestead, provided you met the ownership and occupancy tests by December 1 of the preceding year. Forms are on the Assessor's page or at the office, 507-457-6300.

Which Cook County offices send and collect the tax bill?

Valuation sits with the County Assessor. Billing and collection sit with the Auditor-Treasurer. Both keep desks in the courthouse at 411 W. 2nd Street, Grand Marais, the county seat.

Dial 218-387-3650 for the Assessor about a value, a class, a homestead filing or an inspection visit. Dial 218-387-3640 for the Auditor-Treasurer about a statement, a payment or old unpaid years. The county portal takes current-year payments once amounts are figured in late March, while back taxes from earlier years have to be handled by phone.

What does Cook County look like to a house seller?

Minnesota's far northeastern tip belongs to Cook County, a wooded wedge pressed between Lake Superior and the Canadian line. It holds 1,452.57 square miles of land and about 5,522 people on the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, so roughly four residents share each square mile.

  • Named places include Grand Marais, Hovland, Grand Portage, Tofte, Schroeder and Lutsen.
  • There are 6,251 housing units but just 2,710 households, and the 2020 census found 54.3% of units empty, which shows how many cabins and second homes are mixed into the stock.
  • Year-round owners live in 77.7% of occupied homes, and those homes have a typical value of $336,200 (2020 to 2024).
  • Households bring in a typical $72,638 a year, and 35.3% of people are past 65.

The county is the state's second largest by area, with 57% of its 3,340 square miles under water, and the Grand Portage Indian Reservation lies within it. Eagle Mountain, at 2,301 feet, is the highest natural point in Minnesota. Wikipedia counts 116 days a year below freezing.

Buyers here are few and often seasonal, so a cabin or lakeshore lot can carry a very different tax picture from a year-round house in town. Pull your statement before you set a price.

When does Cook County collect, and what do late payments add?

Real estate tax comes in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and the Assessor's calendar gives November 15 as the second-half date for agricultural land. Both 2026 real estate dates have gone by, so a balance from this year is already growing.

State law (Minnesota Statutes 279.01) adds 2% to a late homestead bill and 4% to a late nonhomestead bill right after the date, then adds more at the start of each later month, with caps of 8% and 12%. The Auditor-Treasurer can quote the exact payoff for any year.

  • A bill of $100 or less is paid whole on the first-half date.
  • When the statement missed the April 25 postmark cutoff, the first half is due 21 days after it was mailed.
  • An owner whose mailed check carries a postmark within one business day of the deadline gets a one-time penalty abatement.
  • A National Guard or reserve member on federal active duty gets four extra months, with a copy of orders attached.

If you are selling, ask the Auditor-Treasurer for a payoff on your closing date, because the county holds the final number for each parcel.

Which dates on the Cook County assessment calendar matter most?

The Assessor publishes a year-round calendar. These entries affect an owner or a seller choosing when to list.

Selected Cook County, MN property tax dates (Cook County Assessor calendar)
DateWhat happens
January 2Assessment date for real and personal property
On or before March 31Auditor-Treasurer mails tax statements
March to MayAssessor mails market value notices, at least 10 days before the local board meets
April 1 to May 31Local boards of appeal and equalization meet
April 30Last day to file a Tax Court petition on current taxes
May 15 and October 15First and second half of real property tax due
Last 10 meeting days of June after the second FridayCounty Board of Appeal and Equalization convenes
November 24 (on or before)Notices of proposed taxes mailed
December 31Homestead and disabled veteran applications due

How do you contest a Cook County value?

Call the Assessor first, and go before the Cook County Board of Appeal and Equalization only if that talk fails. The board's own notice says an appointment is required to present an appeal, and written comments can be handed to the Assessor to read on your behalf.

  • Collect sales of similar homes, an appraisal, or repair quotes that show a defect the Assessor could not see from the road.
  • Call 218-387-3650 ahead of the board meeting, since many disputes end at that desk.
  • Look at your valuation notice for the June meeting time.
  • If the board leaves the value standing, you can petition the Minnesota Tax Court or the district court. Section 278.01 puts the filing deadline for that petition and its proof of service at April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

The Assessor also has to inspect every property at least once in five years. The 2026 review area, tied to the January 2, 2027 assessment, covers Lutsen, Tofte and Schroeder, and inspection visits there are booked by phone.

How does a Cook County sale deal with the tax bill?

The deed will not be recorded until the auditor confirms the land has no delinquent tax. Section 272.12 has the auditor check the books and mark the deed "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered"; without that mark the recorder refuses it.

Two more items travel with a sale. Any price above $3,000 calls for a certificate of real estate value (section 272.115). A deed that carves off only part of a tax parcel also needs the treasurer's certification that the current year's tax on the full parcel is paid (section 272.121). The sale ends the seller's homestead too, since the Assessor drops the class for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies.

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer which years are open on your parcel before you accept an offer.

Which Cook County filing dates can catch an owner off guard?

Several relief filings have fixed cutoffs. A homestead application must reach the Assessor by December 31 to count for the following year, and disabled veteran exclusion filings use the same day. Owners who are blind or permanently and totally disabled have until October 1 for the special homestead class, and a senior citizen deferral request is due July 1.

The Property Tax Refund form M-1PR is due August 15. Resort owners file a declaration by January 15, and a 2c managed forest application is due April 30. Ask the Assessor which of these apply to your parcel.

More questions about Cook County, MN Property Tax Guide

Is this the same Cook County as Chicago?

No. This page covers Cook County, Minnesota, on the north shore of Lake Superior, with Grand Marais as county seat. Its property tax offices are the Assessor at 218-387-3650 and the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640.

When is the next Cook County property tax payment due?

The 2026 halves, May 15 and October 15, are past, so the next real estate date is the first-half deadline in May 2027, for taxes payable in 2027. Agricultural land used November 15 for its second half this year. Statements are mailed on or before March 31.

Can I pay delinquent Cook County taxes online?

No. The county says delinquent taxes for prior years cannot be paid online, only current-year taxes once the amounts are calculated in late March. Call the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 to get a payoff amount for each open year, and ask about any partial payment before you send money.

Can I still appeal my Cook County value this year?

The 2026 local and county board meetings are over. A Tax Court or district court petition on taxes payable in 2027 must be filed by April 30, 2027, and you should talk to the assessor first. Call 218-387-3650.

Do I have to pay off the tax before selling a Cook County house?

Delinquent tax must be cleared before the deed can be recorded, and the auditor stamps the deed once that is done. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 for the amount owed on your parcel before you accept an offer.

Selling in Redwood County?

Which Redwood County offices deal with your tax bill?

Everything runs through the Redwood County Government Center at 403 South Mill Street in Redwood Falls. Valuation and classification belong to the Assessor, reached at 507-637-4008, and Jesse Jacobson holds that post. Billing and collection belong to the Auditor-Treasurer, Jean Price, at 507-637-4013. The Recorder, Amy Gewerth, files deeds at 507-637-4032.

Letters go to P.O. Box 130, Redwood Falls, MN 56283. Phone lines at the assessor's desk stay open weekdays until 4:30 p.m.

What is the housing market like in Redwood County?

Redwood County spreads across 882 square miles of rolling cropland in southwest Minnesota. The Minnesota River marks its northeastern border, the Redwood River runs east through the upper part, and the Cottonwood River crosses the lower part. The ground slopes eastward from a high point of 1,450 feet in the southwest corner. Lawmakers carved out the county in 1862 and took its name from the Redwood River.

Redwood Falls, the seat, had 5,102 residents in 2020 and joined with North Redwood in 1996. U.S. Highway 71 runs through it, joined by highways 19 and 67. Fourteen smaller cities share the county: Belview, Clements, Delhi, Lamberton, Lucan, Milroy, Morgan, Revere, Sanborn, Seaforth, Vesta, Wabasso, Walnut Grove and Wanda. The Lower Sioux Indian Reservation lies entirely inside the county, in Paxton and Sherman townships.

Redwood Falls grew from a claim staked in 1864 by Samuel McPhail, who donated land for the courthouse in 1872 when the town became the seat. John Honner built a house in North Redwood in 1869 that still stands and carries a federal historic listing. The city took over Alexander Ramsey Park from the state in 1958, and it is the largest municipal park in Minnesota.

Housing figures from Census Bureau QuickFacts:

  • 15,265 people in July 2025, which is 1.0% fewer than the 2020 base count.
  • A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $158,200 (2020 to 2024 figures).
  • Owners live in 78.4% of homes, and renters pay a median of $757 a month.
  • Seven building permits in all of 2025, and 7,133 housing units counted.

The 2020 census counted 7,086 housing units, with 10.8% vacant and 21.4% of occupied homes rented, and 70.1% of residents lived in rural areas. The county shares borders with Renville, Brown, Cottonwood, Murray, Lyon and Yellow Medicine Counties. At these prices, even a modest balance of back tax or penalty is a real line item on a closing statement.

When are Redwood County property taxes due in 2026?

Real estate tax comes due in mid-May and mid-October, and both of those 2026 dates are behind us. One deadline remains this year, tomorrow: agricultural land and manufactured homes owe the second half on Monday, November 16.

Redwood County 2026 property tax due dates, from the Auditor/Treasurer page
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estateFriday, May 15Thursday, October 15
Agricultural real estateFriday, May 15Monday, November 16
Personal propertyFriday, May 15None
Manufactured homeMonday, August 31Monday, November 16

Late payment penalties come from Minnesota Statutes section 279.01 and differ for homestead and nonhomestead land. The county also bills $30 for any bounced check, failed electronic payment or reversed payment.

What payment options does the Redwood County Auditor-Treasurer offer?

The county has an online payments page with a tax parcel lookup, and the Government Center accepts payments over the counter or through the post. A Direct Payment Plan pulls the amount from your checking or savings account, either twice a year or in one annual draft. Call 507-637-4013 to enroll.

Escrow customers should still read the statement. Before closing, request a payoff figure for the parcel from the same office, which also publishes the yearly delinquent tax list and notices of forfeited property sales and sales with unclaimed surplus.

How does the Redwood County assessor arrive at your value?

Every parcel gets a classification based on how it is used and an estimated market value fixed as of January 2. Appraisers walk each property on a five year cycle under Minnesota Statutes section 273.01, and tax-exempt parcels on a six year cycle. A new addition can bring an earlier visit.

The annual notice in spring shows that value and class, and it sets the tax for the following year. Details that affect homestead treatment:

  • On January 2 or December 1, the owner or a qualifying relative has to be living there.
  • The application deadline is December 31 of the assessment year, filed with the Assessor.
  • People who are blind or permanently disabled may apply for a separate class.
  • The disabled veterans' homestead exclusion form and special agricultural homestead forms come from the Assessor's office.

What is the process for contesting a Redwood County valuation?

Start by phoning the assessor about the notice. Failing that, the next stop is the local board of appeal and equalization for your city or township. The Assessor's office hosts those meetings in April, and the 2024 round ran from April 8 to April 24. In most cases you must be heard locally before your case can reach the commissioners.

The county board met on June 16, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. in the Commissioner's Room. Its agenda that evening was one parcel, and the commissioners voted unanimously to deny the change. Beyond the boards, a petition to district court or Tax Court under section 278.01 is the last route, and it has an April 30 filing date.

What if Redwood County tax is unpaid when you want to sell?

Tax still open in early January turns delinquent under section 279.02, with an extra 2% added right away. The tax matters at closing for a second reason: the auditor must mark a deed with a no-delinquent-tax note before the Recorder accepts it under section 272.12. Probate distribution deeds and transfer on death deeds are among the listed exceptions.

In practice the title agent subtracts what you owe from your proceeds, so a quick call to the Auditor-Treasurer keeps surprises out of the closing statement.

Which Redwood County recording tools help before a sale?

The Recorder's page describes three. LandShark is a web tool for searching land records and viewing document images, and an account needs a signed web portal agreement with an original wet signature plus a set-up fee. Land Notification emails you when anything is filed against your personal or business name, so a surprise lien shows up quickly. The eCRV tool is where the sale certificate gets filed, and the county says paper certificates have not been accepted for sales since October 1, 2014.

After closing, the assessor drops homestead classification on the sold property for the next assessment year unless the buyer applies and qualifies, per section 272.115.

More questions about Redwood County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the last Redwood County tax deadline of 2026?

Monday, November 16, 2026, covering the second half on agricultural property and manufactured homes. Standard real estate second halves came due October 15.

Who can I call about a Redwood County home value I think is too high?

Call the County Assessor at 507-637-4008. If the answer does not satisfy you, the next steps are the local board in April and the county board in June.

Can a Redwood County house be sold with property tax still owing?

Yes. The balance has to be cleared before the Recorder will file the deed, and it normally comes out of the seller's proceeds. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-637-4013 for the exact payoff.

What is the Redwood County homestead application deadline?

December 31 of the assessment year. The home must be owned and occupied by the owner or a qualifying relative as of January 2 or December 1.

Will the buyer automatically get my Redwood County homestead status?

No. After a transfer the assessor removes homestead for the following assessment year unless the new owner files an application and qualifies.

Who do I contact about property tax in Swift County?

The Auditor-Treasurer's Office in the courthouse at 301 14th Street North in Benson handles bills and payments, and the Assessor handles value and class. Mail goes to P.O. Box 207, Benson, MN 56215. The office phone is 320-843-4069, and the Treasurer's line for the online tax search is 320-843-3544.

The county Assessor page explains an unusual split. The 21 townships contract with local assessors, while the eight cities and villages contract with the County Assessor. A rural seller may therefore be dealing with a township assessor, and a seller in Benson or Appleton with the county office. Your valuation notice or the county can tell you which assessor set your value.

The Auditor-Treasurer also keeps tax forfeiture sale listings, takes automatic withdrawal forms and posts a real estate tax search. Swift County's Land Records Office, which files deeds, is a separate counter in the same courthouse.

What is Swift County like for someone selling a house?

Swift County is a quiet farm county in west central Minnesota with Benson as its seat and largest city. It covers 752 square miles, 742 of them land, arranged as three tiers of seven townships. The Minnesota River bends along the lower west border, the Pomme de Terre River crosses the west, and the Chippewa River runs through the middle. Monson Lake State Park, Swift Falls Park and the Appleton OHV Park are public outdoor spaces.

The legislature set up the county on February 18, 1870, from part of Chippewa County, and named it for Henry Adoniram Swift, the third governor of Minnesota. The St. Paul and Pacific Railroad reached Benson in 1870 and placed its trading centers about eight miles apart. The courthouse dates to 1897 and is on the National Register of Historic Places. The cities today are Appleton, Benson, Clontarf, Danvers, De Graff, Holloway, Kerkhoven and Murdock.

The economy is mostly farming, with some farm equipment manufacturing and an ethanol plant. Adjacent counties are Stevens, Pope, Kandiyohi, Chippewa, Lac qui Parle and Big Stone.

What do the Census numbers say about Swift County homes?

Swift County has about 9,800 residents, and the median is only a midpoint for homes that vary widely between town lots and farmsteads. The table lists the Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures.

Swift County housing and population figures, Census QuickFacts

How does a Swift County homestead get approved?

You must own and live in the home by December 1 and file the application by December 15. The Assessor's page states that rule and says applications are available at the Assessor's Office. Without a homestead classification the property is taxed at a nonhomestead rate, which also means a higher late penalty under Minnesota Statutes 279.01.

The same page lists what the county assessor does for a city parcel:

  • Finds and lists taxable property and sets its use and classification.
  • Estimates market value by studying sales and mails the owner a notice each year.
  • Decides which parcels qualify for homestead.
  • Gives realtors, appraisers and others public information on request.

The county adds that a bill can change because of township, city, school or county budgets, voter-approved school levies, special assessments such as ditch, sewer and street projects, and changes made by the Minnesota Legislature.

When are Swift County property taxes due?

The first half is due May 15 and the second half on October 15, with agricultural land given until November 15. The county's automatic withdrawal form uses those three dates, and Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets them.

A half that misses its date gets a 2 percent penalty on homestead property or 4 percent on nonhomestead property, with more added on the first of each following month. A tract with taxes of $100 or less owes the full amount with the first half. The treasurer must abate a late penalty one time if the payment is postmarked within one business day of the due date.

The county's tax search can be reached from the real estate taxes page. If the search will not load, call the Treasurer's Office at 320-843-3544. A delinquency notice costs $10 per parcel for publication under the county fee schedule, and a Confession of Judgment payment plan is $250 per parcel, so catching up before the notice is worth the effort. A tax search on one parcel costs $2.

What if a Swift County owner falls behind on taxes before selling?

Pay what you can and call the courthouse, because Minnesota lets the county treasurer take a partial payment and apply it to the oldest unpaid installment first. Any shortfall is then charged to penalty before tax. The Auditor-Treasurer's Office at 320-843-4069 can state the exact payoff, including accrued penalty and any publication charge.

The county keeps a page titled Taxes, Delinquent and Forfeiture, and it routes questions about forfeiture sale listings to that same number. A seller who is behind should settle the balance, or arrange a payment plan, before a closing date is set. A Veteran's Services office also sits in the courthouse basement and is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. for owners who want help with benefits that could affect household finances.

What does a Swift County deed or sale cost to record?

The county fee schedule lists the recording costs, and the largest is the deed tax. The state-set deed tax is the purchase price times 0.0033, and a mortgage registration tax is the loan amount times 0.0023. The Land Records section of the schedule also shows these.

  • Well disclosure certificate: $54.
  • Plat: $56.
  • State tax lien release: $30.
  • Certified copy: $10, and attested copy: $2.
  • Torrens original certificate of title: $46.

Land Records is also the Registrar of Titles for Torrens property, which is registered land, and the office says the Registrar must check documents before issuing a certificate of title. The Land Records page notes that county records go back to the 1870s, that the first Register of Deeds took office in 1871 and that Minnesota's race-notice rule means the first to record gains priority. If a deed is going on, file it promptly and ask whether the parcel is abstract or Torrens before you prepare it.

What local permits might affect a Swift County sale?

Rural parcels can involve county zoning permits, and the fee schedule posts them. A dwelling, addition, mobile home or cabin permit is $50, a sewage permit $100, a variance $250 and a conditional use permit $500. The 2026 E911 address fee is $151. These costs matter if a buyer plans to build, add on or change the use of land.

Environmental Services issues the permits, and the county lists applications and feedlot reports under that department. Ask for the zoning district and any feedlot or ditch record when you list acreage.

More questions about Swift County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the phone number for the Swift County Auditor-Treasurer?

320-843-4069 for the Auditor-Treasurer, and 320-843-3544 for the Treasurer's Office. Both are at the courthouse, 301 14th Street North, Benson.

When is the Swift County homestead deadline?

You must own and occupy the home by December 1 and apply by December 15. The Assessor's Office has the application.

Which Swift County cities use the county assessor?

The county says the eight cities and villages contract with the County Assessor, while the 21 townships use local assessors. The cities are Appleton, Benson, Clontarf, Danvers, De Graff, Holloway, Kerkhoven and Murdock.

How much is Minnesota deed tax in Swift County?

The county's fee schedule shows deed tax as the purchase price times 0.0033. A well disclosure certificate adds $54 when one is needed.

Does Swift County offer automatic tax withdrawals?

Yes. The Auditor-Treasurer posts a property tax automatic withdrawal form that draws on May 15, October 15 for nonagricultural parcels and November 15 for agricultural parcels.

Nobles County, MN Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Minnesota
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Nobles County, MN Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Nobles County, MN Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Nobles County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Nobles County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Nobles County

  • Nobles County Auditor-Treasurer

Tax rate

Selling in Nobles County?
We buy Nobles County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where do Nobles County property owners get tax answers?

The Government Center at 315 Tenth Street in Worthington houses both offices you will need. The Auditor-Treasurer answers at 507-295-5258 and takes mail at PO Box 757, Worthington, MN 56187. The Assessor is at 507-295-5208. The Auditor-Treasurer page calls that office the county's property tax administrator and a statutory member of the County Board of Equalization.

The office also handles some items that rarely appear in other counties' summaries: wind energy and transmission line taxes, ditch fund assessments, tax increment financing and mobile home transfers. For a house seller the useful pieces are collecting current and delinquent tax, special assessments and forfeiture proceedings.

The Assessor's page lists forms for homestead, general exemption, blind or disabled homestead and the disabled veteran exclusions. The homestead form is the one an owner-occupant files with this office.

What kind of county is Nobles County for a home seller?

Nobles County is in the southwest corner of Minnesota against the Iowa border, on the Buffalo Ridge, where hills reach about 1,995 feet. The county was created in 1857 and organized in 1870, with Worthington platted in 1871 and named seat in 1873. Eleven cities share the map, among them Adrian, Brewster, Ellsworth, Round Lake and Wilmont. Lake Okabena and Lake Ocheda sit in the county, and farming leads the economy, with corn, soybeans and hogs, followed by food processing and metal fabrication.

QuickFacts numbers for the county:

  • 22,338 people in July 2025, only 0.2% above the 2020 base
  • 8,417 housing units, 74.2% owner-occupied
  • Median owner-occupied value of $197,200 and median gross rent of $896
  • 2.80 people per household, and 28.6% of residents under 18
  • 38.3% Hispanic or Latino, with 34.6% of people age 5 and over speaking a language other than English at home
  • Median household income of $66,101 and 94 building permits in 2025

Carrying costs are modest by state standards: median selected monthly owner costs run $1,456 with a mortgage and $590 without one. Per-person income is $31,342, and 13.3% of residents are below the poverty line, so a large unexpected tax or assessment bill lands harder here than the headline home value suggests. The county posts local tax rates and proposed levies on its property tax page, so you can see what the next bill is built from.

When do Nobles County property taxes fall due in 2026?

The county's own 2026 calendar splits dates by property type, which is different from the single mid-October date many owners expect:

Nobles County 2026 payment calendar as posted by the Auditor-Treasurer
DateWhat is due
May 15, 2026All taxes, first half
August 31, 2026Mobile home taxes, first half
October 15, 2026City taxes, second half, if applicable
November 16, 2026Farm taxes and mobile home taxes, second half, if applicable

November 15 falls on a Sunday this year, which is why the farm date reads November 16. The second half is not mailed, so keep the first-half stub. The county processes payments within 24 hours of receipt. If you are late, call the office at 507-295-5258 to learn the penalty to include, since the state sets it under section 279.01: 2% on homestead and 4% on other property for the first missed date, rising monthly to caps of 8% and 12%.

What are the ways to pay in Nobles County?

The county lists six methods on its property tax page:

  • Mail a check payable to Nobles County Auditor-Treasurer with the stub from every parcel; the postmark must be on or before the due date
  • Direct payment plan, which pulls the amount from a checking or savings account until you cancel
  • Online by card or e-check, with convenience fees
  • In person at the Government Center by check, cash or card
  • The drop box outside the main entrance on the 10th Street side, open around the clock
  • Escrow through a mortgage lender, which applies when the lender's name appears at the top of the statement

The county will not take post-dated checks, and a private postage meter mark does not prove timely mailing. The office also reminds owners that liability for the tax stands even if a statement never arrives.

How do I contest my Nobles County valuation?

Only the estimated market value for the current assessment year can be contested, according to the Board of Appeal and Equalization handbook posted by the county, and the number is struck as of January 2. Rather than the tax amount, the board reviews the value and class behind it. Call the Assessor first to check the facts on your notice.

  1. Go to your local board, or the open book session if your area holds one. Valuation notices must be mailed at least 10 days beforehand.
  2. If the result still looks wrong, take it to the County Board of Equalization. In 2026 it met on June 16 at 6:00 PM, and the board may sit up to 10 consecutive meeting days in June after the second Friday.
  3. File with the Minnesota Tax Court or district court by April 30 of the year the tax is payable, per section 278.01.

Neither board can grant special program status, such as Green Acres. Those need their own application, and a board may not give relief to an owner who refused the assessor entry to inspect.

Which towns and neighbors border a Nobles County property?

Beyond Worthington, the county's cities are Adrian, Bigelow, Brewster, Dundee, Ellsworth, Kinbrae, Lismore, Round Lake, Rushmore and Wilmont, and Leota is a census-designated place. Org, Pfingsten, Ransom, Reading and St. Kilian are unincorporated communities. Murray, Cottonwood, Jackson and Rock counties adjoin it in Minnesota, with Osceola and Lyon counties across the line in Iowa.

The county has a long list of state wildlife management areas and county parks, among them Adrian Spring County Park, Hawkeye County Park and the Lake Bella and Fulda wildlife areas. Prairieland Transit serves the county. Where your house sits matters for the tax bill, because the school district, city or township levy on the statement changes with the address even when the county levy is the same.

What should a Nobles County seller check before closing?

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer for any balance on the parcel, since delinquent tax and unpaid special assessments surface at transfer. Under section 272.12, the auditor looks up delinquent tax when a deed arrives, and the recorder refuses a deed lacking the "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered" stamp.

The office lists tax forfeiture proceedings among its duties, and its property tax page links to a list of tax forfeiture property. Selling well ahead of that stage keeps the decision with you. If your lender collects through escrow, ask the lender how the escrow balance will be handled at payoff, and ask the Auditor-Treasurer whether the second half has been paid.

More questions about Nobles County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the phone number for Nobles County property taxes?

Call 507-295-5258 for the Auditor-Treasurer, who collects tax. The Assessor, who sets value and class, is at 507-295-5208. Both are in the Government Center at 315 Tenth Street, Worthington.

Why is the farm tax date November 16 in 2026?

The usual agricultural date of November 15 lands on a Sunday this year. Nobles County posts November 16, 2026 for farm and mobile home second-half payments, so the deadline moves to Monday.

Does Nobles County mail second-half tax statements?

No. The county does not mail second-half statements, so you must keep the stub from the first mailing. Taxpayers remain responsible for payment even when no statement reaches them.

Can I use the drop box for a late-night payment?

Yes. The drop box outside the Government Center's main entrance on 10th Street is accessible 24 hours a day. A mailed payment instead needs a postmark on or before the due date.

Can I appeal a Nobles County tax bill amount?

You can contest the estimated market value or classification, not the tax amount itself. Start with the Assessor, then the local board or open book, then the County Board, and file any Tax Court petition by April 30.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Douglas County, MN Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Douglas County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Douglas County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Douglas County

  • Douglas County Auditor/Treasurer

Tax rate

Selling in Douglas County?
We buy Douglas County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Douglas County by the numbers

Who handles property tax in Douglas County, Minnesota?

Two offices share the work. The Assessor's Office values and classifies about 30,000 parcels, and the Auditor/Treasurer calculates, bills and collects the tax. Both are in Alexandria, and the assessor's FAQ lists county hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Assessor: 305 8th Avenue West, 2nd floor, Alexandria, MN 56308. Phone 320-762-3884, email assessors.office@co.douglas.mn.us.
  • Auditor/Treasurer: 821 Cedar Street, Alexandria, MN 56308. Phone 320-762-3077, tax email taxdept@co.douglas.mn.us.

The county's Parcel Info Lookup gives you the tax statement and the value notice by parcel. Some assessment districts in Douglas County hire their own local assessor under contract, so call the county office if you want to know who actually viewed your house.

What kind of county is Douglas County for a house seller?

Douglas County is a lake county in west-central Minnesota with Alexandria as both seat and largest city. The county was created in 1858 and organized in 1866, and it is named for Stephen A. Douglas. Roughly 83 of its 720 square miles are water, with more than 250 lakes. Lake Carlos State Park is inside the county, and it holds Minnesota's only wine-grape appellation, the Alexandria Lakes AVA.

Other cities are Brandon, Carlos, Evansville, Forada, Garfield, Kensington, Millerville, Miltona, Nelson and part of Osakis. The 2020 census counted 39,006 people, and the Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 40,120.

QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows a median owner-occupied value of $321,400, an owner-occupied rate of 76.5 percent, a median household income of $79,043 and 17,519 households. The county had 23,040 housing units in 2025 and issued 319 building permits that year. The 2020 count of housing units showed 23.9 percent vacant, a figure that can include seasonal lake homes. That matters for sellers because the county assessor classifies seasonal residential property separately from year-round homes.

When are Douglas County property taxes due?

Real estate tax comes due in two halves, May 15 and October 15, and the county says the postmark counts. Agricultural property and mobile homes have a later second-half date of November 15, while mobile home first-half tax is due August 31.

A missed deadline brings a 2 percent penalty on homestead and 4 percent on non-homestead property (Minn. Stat. 279.01).

Douglas County tax payment dates. Sources: Douglas County Auditor/Treasurer page; Minn. Stat. 279.01.
Tax typeFirst paymentSecond payment
Real estateMay 15October 15
AgriculturalMay 15November 15
Mobile homeAugust 31November 15

How can I pay my Douglas County tax bill?

The Auditor/Treasurer lists five ways to pay: an ACH direct payment plan, a drop box, online credit card or virtual check, mail, or a visit to the office. The office moved from the courthouse to the Administration Building, so older directions to the courthouse no longer apply.

  • Drop boxes: one on the west side of the Administration Building and a drive-through box in the parking lot, both at 821 Cedar Street.
  • Online: reached from the county website through the parcel lookup.
  • ACH: the county's direct payment plan debits your account on the due dates.

To have a duplicate statement mailed, call 320-762-3077. For a copy of the value notice, call the assessor at 320-762-3884.

How are Douglas County values set and what moves them?

Values are set as of January 2 each year, and sales are the main driver. The assessor compares sale prices with assessed values to check each district against state standards, then mails every owner a notice of value and classification in the spring. There are five classes: residential, seasonal, apartment, agricultural and commercial/industrial, and each property is either homestead or non-homestead.

The county's own summary for the 2024 assessment said every district would see an increase, and that lakefront was the hot segment: 114 lake sales averaged $580,000, up 17 percent, with front-foot values on the chain of lakes running between $400 and $600 depending on the lake. The same notice explains that a higher value does not by itself raise your bill. Your taxable market value is multiplied by the class rate to find your share of the levy that the county, city or township and school district have set.

The assessor's FAQ also lists what does and does not push value up. Minor repairs such as a new roof, porch repair, original siding, paint or replaced plumbing and electrical fixtures usually will not raise the estimated market value alone, although several together could. Fire or storm damage should be reported, since the assessment date is January 2.

How do I appeal a Douglas County assessment?

Call the assessor first at 320-762-3884. Formal appeals happen in order, and the June county board only hears you if the local board or open book meeting heard you first.

  1. Local board or open book. The county's 2024 notice scheduled these for April 9 through April 19, by appointment. Your valuation notice names the date and place for your district, and Alexandria has its own city board.
  2. County Board of Appeal and Equalization. This meets in June.
  3. Minnesota Tax Court. The petition is filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01).

Meetings cannot change the tax statement you are paying now. They only affect the next one. Owners who struggle with a homestead bill can check the state Department of Revenue's M1PR form, which compares income with property tax due and may give a partial refund.

What does it take to qualify for homestead in Douglas County?

You must occupy the property as your primary residence, be one of its owners or a relative of an owner, and be a Minnesota resident. The assessor's FAQ points to voter registration, driver's license, income tax forms and vehicle registration as records that should show the homestead address.

This is worth checking before a sale in a lake county. A cottage that a family treats as a second home is a seasonal class, and the class rate differs from a year-round homestead. If the buyer plans to live in the house, the assessor will need a fresh application from them, so give the buyer the assessor's number, 320-762-3884, early in the process.

Moving also means updating the mailing address on the tax record. Douglas County has a Taxpayer Address Change Request Form that can be emailed or mailed to the Auditor-Treasurer's Office at 821 Cedar Street, so the next statement reaches the right owner.

What happens to the tax when a Douglas County house sells?

The county auditor must see that no delinquent tax sits on the land before a deed can be recorded (Minn. Stat. 272.12). Ask the closing agent for the tax payoff before the signing date, and ask how the current half-year is divided between you and the buyer under your purchase agreement.

New buyers who want homestead need to apply, because all new homesteads require an application, and owners who live in their house but are not getting homestead status should contact the assessor. Taxes left unpaid long enough can end in forfeiture. The Auditor/Treasurer's page says forfeited property goes to the state after the redemption period ends, and that period has been three years since January 1, 2014, down from five.

More questions about Douglas County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the Douglas County Auditor/Treasurer's phone number?

The office number is 320-762-3077, at 821 Cedar Street in Alexandria. Tax questions can also go to taxdept@co.douglas.mn.us, and the county lists regular hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Can I pay Douglas County property tax by drop box?

Yes. There is a box on the west side of the Administration Building and a drive-through box in the parking lot. The county counts the postmark as timely for mailed payments.

Do I need an appointment to appeal a Douglas County value?

Yes, the county has required appointments for local board and open book meetings. Call the assessor at 320-762-3884 or email assessors.office@co.douglas.mn.us, and call the city if you live in Alexandria and want its board.

What is the November tax notice from Douglas County?

It is the proposed tax notice for next year. The county says these are mailed in mid to late November, and they are separate from the statement you receive by March 31.

How long do I have to redeem a Douglas County parcel that went tax forfeit?

The county states a three-year redemption period, shortened from five years effective January 1, 2014. Contact the Auditor/Treasurer at 320-762-3077 before that period ends.

Who to contact in Fillmore County

  • Fillmore County Auditor/Treasurer

Tax rate

Selling in Fillmore County?
We buy Fillmore County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where do I take property tax questions in Fillmore County?

Both offices work from the courthouse at 101 Fillmore Street in Preston, and the county lists Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. for each. The Auditor/Treasurer's Office stays open through the noon hour.

  • Auditor/Treasurer: PO Box 627, Preston, MN 55965. Phone 507-765-3811 or 507-765-4701. Email auditor@fillmorecountymn.gov (the county changed its email addresses on August 18, 2026).
  • Assessor: PO Box 466, Preston, MN 55965. Phone 507-765-3868. The office asks you to allow two business days for an email reply.

The Auditor/Treasurer keeps the tax roll, which means ownership changes, splits, combinations and transfers all pass through that desk. The same office prepares the property tax statements, runs the county's tax-forfeited land sales and offers a property tax search and statement lookup through the Beacon site linked from the county page.

What is Fillmore County like for someone selling a house?

Fillmore County lies along the Iowa border in the southeastern corner of Minnesota, inside the Driftless Area, and it is part of the Rochester metropolitan area. Preston is the county seat, and Spring Valley is the largest city. Rolling hills, gullies and karst topography shape most parcels, and the Root River drains the county, flowing eastward.

The county was created in 1853, named for Millard Fillmore, and drew many Norwegian settlers. By 1860 it was the most populous county in Minnesota. The 2020 census counted 21,228 people, and the Census Bureau classified essentially all of the county's population as rural. Cities include Canton, Chatfield (part), Fountain, Harmony, Lanesboro, Mabel, Ostrander, Peterson, Rushford, Rushford Village, Wykoff and Whalan.

QuickFacts gives a median owner-occupied value of $221,100 and an owner-occupied rate of 82.6 percent for 2020 to 2024, with 9,890 housing units and median household income of $77,512. Only 58 building permits were issued in 2025. Forestville/Mystery Cave State Park lies inside the county, and median gross rent runs $797.

What do Census figures say about Fillmore County homeowners?

The Census Bureau estimates 21,540 residents for July 2025, a gain of 1.5 percent since April 2020. About 24.4 percent are 65 or older, and 92.5 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so most owners stay put for long stretches.

  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 8,723, at 2.40 persons each.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,520 with a mortgage and $588 without one.
  • Mean travel time to work: 25.7 minutes.
  • Persons in poverty: 8.1 percent.

Even without a loan, the typical owner-occupied house in Fillmore County carries about $588 a month in owner costs. A family holding an inherited house for a few months still pays that monthly stream, so ask the auditor for the tax figure early and plan around it.

When is Fillmore County property tax due?

Two installments, mid-May and mid-October, cover residential real estate. Minnesota's statute (Minn. Stat. 279.01) puts the first half due before May 16 and the second before October 16, and the county's own reminders restate October 15 and give farmers and mobile home owners until November 15 for their second half.

One snag is the weekday. In 2021 the county's notice listed May 17 as the first-half date, so check the date printed on your statement rather than relying on a fixed day. If you pay late, the penalty depends on classification: 2 percent for homestead and 4 percent for non-homestead on the day after, growing each month after that.

Fillmore County payment timing. Sources: Fillmore County Auditor/Treasurer notices; Minn. Stat. 279.01.
ItemTiming
First-half real estate taxMid-May (May 15, shifted when it lands on a weekend)
Second-half real estate taxMid-October (October 15)
Second-half farm and mobile home taxNovember 15
Tax Court petition for current taxApril 30 of the year payable
Formal appeal on the valuation noticeLocal board or open book in spring, then county board in June

Can Fillmore County taxes be paid automatically?

Yes. The Auditor/Treasurer offers a no-charge ACH service that pulls property tax from a checking or savings account on the due dates. The county promoted it as a way to avoid late fees tied to postal delays. Call 507-765-3811 or write to the auditor email above to sign up.

Sellers should cancel or update the ACH authorization once the house closes, so the old account is not debited for a bill that belongs to the buyer. Confirm with the office how long a change takes before the next due date.

How does a Fillmore County property tax appeal work?

Call the assessor at 507-765-3868 first. The valuation notice lists the formal options and the dates for your township or city, and the notice is the only place those dates are fixed for the year.

  1. Talk to the assessor. Changes to a value usually come from appraisal work in your jurisdiction or from market adjustments to bring assessment statistics into range.
  2. Local Board of Appeal and Equalization, or open book. If the conversation does not settle things, this is the first formal step. State law keeps these meetings between April 1 and May 31 (Minn. Stat. 274.01).
  3. County Board of Appeal and Equalization. In its 2021 notice, Fillmore County asked owners to contact the assessor ahead of the June meeting to be put on the agenda, and that board met in the commissioners' board room at the courthouse.
  4. Minnesota Tax Court. If those steps fail, the petition is due April 30 of the year the tax is payable (Minn. Stat. 278.01).

The county warns that once the county board adjourns very few options remain, and it recommends bringing written supporting documents. If you refuse the assessor access to the inside of the house, a board cannot give you a value or class change that benefits the property (Minn. Stat. 274.01).

What should I do before closing on a Fillmore County house?

Ask the title agent to run delinquent tax before the deed goes to the auditor. Minnesota law has the auditor check for delinquent tax on the land and certify it, and the recorder may not take the deed without that certificate (Minn. Stat. 272.12).

In a county where much of the land is agricultural, also check whether the parcel is being split or combined, since the auditor maintains those records. Farm owners get a later second-half date, so a farm sale closing between October 15 and November 15 can leave a half-year of tax still open even though no penalty has started. Ask the closing agent and the auditor which half is outstanding.

What happens when tax goes unpaid in Fillmore County?

The Auditor/Treasurer conducts tax-forfeited land sales for the county, which is the end of the road for a parcel whose tax stays unpaid.

If you inherited a house or are behind, call the auditor at 507-765-3811 for the full balance with penalty and interest and for the parcel's status. State law has the treasurer apply any payment to the oldest unpaid installment first (Minn. Stat. 279.01), so a partial payment reduces the oldest year before the current one.

More questions about Fillmore County, MN Property Tax Guide

Where is the Fillmore County Auditor/Treasurer located?

The office is at 101 Fillmore Street in Preston, MN 55965, with mail going to PO Box 627. The phone numbers are 507-765-3811 and 507-765-4701.

Does Fillmore County offer automatic tax payments?

Yes. The county has a no-charge ACH service that takes the payment from a checking or savings account on the due dates. Call 507-765-3811 to enroll.

Who do I call about my Fillmore County property value?

Call the Assessor at 507-765-3868. The office allows two business days for an email response, and the valuation notice you receive describes the next formal appeal steps.

When is the second half due for a Fillmore County farm?

November 15 for agricultural property and mobile homes. Regular residential real estate is due October 15.

Can I search my Fillmore County tax statement online?

Yes. The Auditor/Treasurer page links to a property tax search and statement lookup on the Beacon site.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Le Sueur County, MN Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Le Sueur County, MN Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Le Sueur County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to contact in Le Sueur County

Tax rate

What we could not confirm

  • Due dates and delinquency penalties not on an opened page; office hours truncated

Which Le Sueur County offices handle property tax?

The Assessor values and classifies the land, and the Auditor-Treasurer calculates and collects the tax. The Assessor's office is at 88 S Park Avenue, Le Center, MN 56057, phone 507-357-8213.

According to the county Assessor's page, the staff reviews about 19,000 parcels in 14 townships and 10 cities. They estimate market value, classify property by principal use (residential, agricultural, seasonal or commercial) and decide which parcels qualify for homestead. Annual sales studies compare the assessor's values with actual sales, and the Minnesota Department of Revenue requires the estimate to land between 90% and 105% of actual market value.

On the tax side, the Property Tax Info page explains that each taxing district certifies its levy, and the Auditor-Treasurer turns those levies into a bill for each owner using the Assessor's values and the state's classifications. The same office processes real estate transactions for property in the county.

What is Le Sueur County like for a home seller?

Le Sueur County sits in south central Minnesota along the Minnesota River and belongs to the Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington metropolitan area. It covers 449 square miles of land, with low rolling hills, lakes and rich black soil.

The county was created on March 5, 1853 and named for the French explorer Pierre-Charles Le Sueur. Its seat has moved several times. Le Sueur was the first seat, Cleveland held it briefly in 1875 to 1876, and Le Sueur Center, renamed Le Center in 1930, has had it since 1876. Cities include Le Center, Le Sueur (partly), Montgomery, Waterville, Elysian (partly), New Prague (partly), Cleveland, Kasota, Kilkenny and Heidelberg, with part of Mankato also reaching in.

The Census Bureau lists 29,453 residents in July 2025, up 2.8% from the 2020 base of 28,663. The Census median for an owner-occupied home is $316,500, the highest of the four counties covered in this series, and median household income is $94,968.

  • Housing units in July 2025: 13,256, with 67 building permits during 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 81.0%.
  • Median gross rent: $942.
  • Mean commute: 24.6 minutes.

How rural is Le Sueur County, and does that affect a sale?

Le Sueur County is overwhelmingly rural by the 2020 census count: 85.8% of residents lived in rural areas and 14.2% in urban ones. There were 11,287 households and 12,811 housing units, of which 11.9% were vacant, and the median age was 41.5.

The Minnesota River forms the west border and the land slopes north and east. Neighbors are Scott County to the north, Rice to the east, Waseca to the south, Blue Earth and Nicollet to the southwest and west, and Sibley to the northwest. Public land includes Sakatah Lake State Park and Seven Mile Creek State Park (both partly in the county), part of the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge, and a string of state wildlife management areas.

  • The county has 14 townships and 10 cities, and the same Assessor's office reviews all of them.
  • Acreage and agricultural land are classified by use, and the Assessor sets that classification.
  • Agricultural, seasonal and residential are separate classes, so a lake or farm parcel can be taxed differently from a house in town.

Census data shows 94.6% of adults 25 and older finished high school and 26.3% hold a bachelor's degree, with 89.2% of households subscribing to broadband.

How do I pay a Le Sueur County property tax bill?

The county accepts cash, check, money order, credit or debit card, and ACH. A 2.5% convenience fee is added when a card is run, and a third-party processor handles those payments.

The county's Beacon mapping application lets the public look up a property, view a map and pay taxes online. Beacon also offers subscription services for name searches and comparable property searches. A single-family property tax calculator spreadsheet, certified tax rates for 2025 and 2026, and levy history sit on the same Property Tax Info page, so you can see how much of a bill comes from each taxing district before you list.

The due dates printed on your statement are the ones that count, and the statewide rule is summarized in the next section.

What are the statewide due dates and penalties that apply in Le Sueur County?

Minnesota law sets two payments: the first half before May 16 and the second before October 16, when a bill exceeds $100. Smaller bills are due in one payment on the first date.

Penalty steps under Minnesota Statutes 279.01
StepHomesteadNonhomestead
Unpaid at due date2%4%
Still unpaid first day of next monthAdditional 2%Additional 4%
Each later month through December1% more1% more
Maximum8%12%

Source: Minnesota Statutes section 279.01. If the property tax statement was mailed after April 24, the first half is due 21 days after the postmark and penalties follow that later date.

How does a valuation appeal work in Le Sueur County?

The Assessor mails a valuation notice to every owner each March, and that notice names the local Board of Appeal and Equalization where you can object.

The county's board schedule shows the 2026 Board of Appeal and Equalization met on Tuesday, June 16 at 6:30 p.m. at the Le Sueur County Government Center and has passed. The county posts later dates on its Local Board of Appeal and Equalization Schedule page.

If you take the dispute to court, Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 requires a petition served on the county auditor and filed with the district court administrator by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. A Tax Court appeal can begin once the valuation notice arrives and must start before May 1. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer whether a minimum payment is required before you file.

Is there any relief for Le Sueur County homeowners?

Yes. The Property Tax Info page leads with the state property tax refund, which is meant for people whose tax is relatively high compared with household income. The Minnesota Department of Revenue says the refund is due August 15 and can be filed up to one year after the due date.

The Assessor decides which parcels qualify for homestead classification, and the penalty table above shows homestead owners start at a lower rate. If you have moved out or the house is empty after an estate, ask the Assessor whether the homestead status ends and when.

What should I check before selling a Le Sueur County house?

Confirm both halves of the current year are paid, get the parcel's special assessment balance, and note the next due date against your closing date. The county handles real estate transactions through the Auditor-Treasurer's office, so a stop there before closing keeps surprises off the settlement statement.

Bring the parcel number, the latest statement and the date you hope to close, and let the Auditor-Treasurer give you the amount to pay through that date.

More questions about Le Sueur County, MN Property Tax Guide

What is the Le Sueur County Assessor's address?

88 S Park Avenue, Le Center, MN 56057, with the phone at 507-357-8213. Le Center is also the county seat.

Does Le Sueur County charge a fee for card payments?

Yes, a 2.5% convenience fee applies when a credit or debit card is run, and it is added to the tax due. Cash, check, money order and ACH are also accepted.

When was the 2026 Le Sueur County board of appeal meeting?

Tuesday, June 16, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. at the Government Center. It has passed, and valuation notices for 2027 are mailed in March.

How many parcels does Le Sueur County have?

Nearly 19,000 parcels in 14 townships and 10 cities, according to the county's property tax and assessor pages.

Can I file for the state property tax refund after August 15?

Yes, for up to one year after the due date, according to the Department of Revenue. The due date is August 15.

Who to contact in Freeborn County

Tax rate

Selling in Freeborn County?
